import TCSlib.Complexity.Formulas.QBFEncoding

set_option maxHeartbeats 0
set_option relaxedAutoImplicit false
set_option autoImplicit false

/-!
# The pure side of the `TQBF` register machine

The facts about quantified formulas that the polynomial-width register machine deciding
`TQBF` (`TCSlib.Complexity.ClassPSPACE.TQBFARM.Walk`) relies on, stated without machines.

* **Syntax.** The finite automaton `Complexity.LogProg.TQBFARM.synStep` (an aligned-pair
  stage followed by the six-state grammar automaton `Std.Sat.CNF.syntaxStep`) accepts exactly
  the encodings `pairEncode qs (CNF.serialize φ)` (`synOK_spec`, `repr_of_synOK`); every other
  string decodes to a true formula (`truth_of_not_synOK`), the fallback convention of
  `Complexity.QBF.decode`.
* **Stack semantics.** The machine keeps the partial assignment of the quantifier prefix as a
  binary stack `S` (a leading `1`, then one bit per bound variable, the innermost lowest);
  `Complexity.LogProg.TQBFARM.asg k S` is the assignment it denotes at depth `k`, and
  `Complexity.LogProg.TQBFARM.Val qs φ k S` the truth value of the remaining formula.
  Pushing a bit is an update of the assignment (`asg_push`), so `Val` obeys the AND/OR
  recursion of [AB09, §4.2, proof of Theorem 4.13] (`val_leaf`, `val_ex`, `val_all`) and is
  the truth of the decoded formula at the root (`val_root`).

Infrastructure for [AB09, §4.2, Theorem 4.13, membership half]; not itself a result of the
book.

## Main definitions

* `Complexity.LogProg.TQBFARM.synStep`, `Complexity.LogProg.TQBFARM.synOK` — the syntax
  automaton and its verdict.
* `Complexity.LogProg.TQBFARM.asg`, `Complexity.LogProg.TQBFARM.Val` — the stack semantics.

## Main results

* `Complexity.LogProg.TQBFARM.truth_of_not_synOK`, `Complexity.LogProg.TQBFARM.repr_of_synOK`.
* `Complexity.LogProg.TQBFARM.val_leaf`, `val_ex`, `val_all`, `val_root`.

## References

* [AB09] S. Arora, B. Barak, *Computational Complexity: A Modern Approach*,
  Cambridge University Press, 2009. (§4.2, Theorem 4.13.)
-/

namespace Complexity.LogProg.TQBFARM

open Std.Sat (CNF)
open Turing

/-! ## Syntax -/

/-- The states of the syntax automaton: during the aligned-pair stage, no bit or the first bit
of a pair (`inl`); after the separator, a state of the grammar automaton (`inr`). -/
abbrev SynSt := Option Bool ⊕ Fin 6

/-- **The syntax automaton**: equal aligned pairs are prefix bits, `01` is the separator into
the grammar automaton `Std.Sat.CNF.syntaxStep`, and `10` enters its error state. -/
def synStep : SynSt → Bool → SynSt
  | .inl none, b => .inl (some b)
  | .inl (some false), false => .inl none
  | .inl (some false), true => .inr 0
  | .inl (some true), true => .inl none
  | .inl (some true), false => .inr 5
  | .inr q, b => .inr (CNF.syntaxStep q b)

/-- The syntax verdict: the automaton ends in the grammar's exact-end state `4`. -/
def synOK (x : List Bool) : Bool :=
  decide (x.foldl synStep (.inl none) = .inr 4)

/-- After the separator the automaton is the grammar automaton. -/
theorem synStep_matrix (x : List Bool) (q : Fin 6) :
    x.foldl synStep (.inr q) = .inr (x.foldl CNF.syntaxStep q) := by
  induction x generalizing q with
  | nil => rfl
  | cons b x ih => exact ih (CNF.syntaxStep q b)

/-- **The syntax automaton accepts exactly a successful pair decoding followed by a successful
matrix parse.**

**Proof sketch.** Follow the recursion of `Turing.pairDecode` two bits at a time: equal pairs
return to the pair stage, `01` hands the rest to the grammar automaton
(`Std.Sat.CNF.syntaxOK_spec`), and `10` or an incomplete pair never reaches state `4`
(`Std.Sat.CNF.syntaxSuffix_run` from the error state). -/
theorem synOK_spec (x : List Bool) :
    synOK x = match pairDecode x with
      | none => false
      | some (_, m) => (CNF.parse m).isSome := by
  induction x using pairDecode.induct with
  | case1 xs ih =>
      change synOK xs = _
      rw [ih]
      cases hp : pairDecode xs <;> simp [pairDecode, hp]
  | case2 xs ih =>
      change synOK xs = _
      rw [ih]
      cases hp : pairDecode xs <;> simp [pairDecode, hp]
  | case3 xs =>
      simp only [synOK, List.foldl_cons, synStep, synStep_matrix, Sum.inr.injEq, pairDecode]
      exact CNF.syntaxOK_spec xs
  | case4 xs h00 h11 h01 =>
      rcases xs with _ | ⟨b, _ | ⟨c, r⟩⟩
      · rfl
      · cases b <;> rfl
      · cases b <;> cases c
        · exact False.elim (h00 r rfl)
        · exact False.elim (h01 r rfl)
        · have herr : r.foldl CNF.syntaxStep 5 ≠ 4 := by
            intro hc
            exact (CNF.syntaxSuffix_run 5 r).mpr hc
          simpa [synOK, synStep, synStep_matrix, pairDecode] using herr
        · exact False.elim (h11 r rfl)

/-- The empty matrix is true under every prefix. -/
theorem truthAux_nil (qs : List QBF.Quant) (σ : ℕ → Bool) (i : ℕ) :
    QBF.truthAux [] qs σ i := by
  induction qs generalizing σ i with
  | nil => rfl
  | cons q qs ih =>
      cases q with
      | ex => exact ⟨false, ih _ _⟩
      | all => exact fun b => ih (Function.update σ i b) (i + 1)

/-- **Rejected strings are true formulas**: a string failing the syntax check decodes to a
fallback with the empty (true) matrix. -/
theorem truth_of_not_synOK {x : List Bool} (h : synOK x = false) : (QBF.decode x).truth := by
  cases hp : pairDecode x with
  | none =>
      simpa [QBF.decode, hp, QBF.truth, CNF.fallback] using truthAux_nil [] (fun _ => false) 0
  | some p =>
      obtain ⟨qs, m⟩ := p
      have hm : CNF.parse m = none := by
        cases he : CNF.parse m with
        | none => rfl
        | some φ => simp [synOK_spec, hp, he] at h
      simpa [QBF.decode, hp, QBF.truth, CNF.decode, hm, CNF.fallback] using
        truthAux_nil (qs.map QBF.quantOfBit) (fun _ => false) 0

/-- **Accepted strings are encodings**: a string passing the syntax check is
`pairEncode qs (CNF.serialize φ)`. -/
theorem repr_of_synOK {x : List Bool} (h : synOK x = true) :
    ∃ (qs : List Bool) (φ : CNF ℕ), x = pairEncode qs (CNF.serialize φ) := by
  rw [synOK_spec] at h
  cases hp : pairDecode x with
  | none => simp [hp] at h
  | some p =>
      obtain ⟨qs, y⟩ := p
      cases hm : CNF.parse y with
      | none => simp [hp, hm] at h
      | some φ =>
          exact ⟨qs, φ, (eq_pairEncode_of_pairDecode x qs y hp).trans
            (congrArg (pairEncode qs) (CNF.parse_repr hm))⟩

/-- The decoding of an encoding: prefix bits read as quantifiers, the matrix recovered. -/
theorem decode_pairEncode (qs : List Bool) (φ : CNF ℕ) :
    QBF.decode (pairEncode qs (CNF.serialize φ)) = ⟨qs.map QBF.quantOfBit, φ⟩ := by
  simp [QBF.decode, pairDecode_pairEncode, CNF.decode_serialize]

/-! ## Stack semantics -/

/-- **The assignment of a stack** `S` at depth `k`: variable `v < k` reads bit `k - 1 - v` of
`S` (the innermost variable is the lowest bit), every other variable reads `false`. -/
def asg (k S : ℕ) : ℕ → Bool :=
  fun v => decide (v < k) && decide (S / 2 ^ (k - 1 - v) % 2 = 1)

/-- At depth `0` every variable reads `false`. -/
theorem asg_zero (S : ℕ) : asg 0 S = fun _ => false := by
  funext v; simp [asg]

/-- **Pushing a bit is an update**: binding variable `k` to `b` in the assignment of `S` at
depth `k` gives the assignment of `2S + b` at depth `k + 1`.

**Proof sketch.** Below `k`, `(2S + b) / 2 ^ (j + 1) = S / 2 ^ j`; at `k` the new lowest bit
is `b`; above, both sides read `false`. -/
theorem asg_push (k S : ℕ) (b : Bool) :
    Function.update (asg k S) k b = asg (k + 1) (2 * S + b.toNat) := by
  funext v
  have hb : b.toNat ≤ 1 := Bool.toNat_le b
  rcases lt_trichotomy v k with h | rfl | h
  · rw [Function.update_of_ne h.ne]
    simp only [asg]
    have e : k + 1 - 1 - v = (k - 1 - v) + 1 := by omega
    rw [e, pow_succ', ← Nat.div_div_eq_div_mul, show (2 * S + b.toNat) / 2 = S by omega]
    simp [h, show v < k + 1 by omega]
  · rw [Function.update_self]
    simp only [asg, show v + 1 - 1 - v = 0 by omega, pow_zero, Nat.div_one]
    cases b <;> simp [Nat.mul_mod_right, Nat.add_mod]
  · rw [Function.update_of_ne h.ne']
    simp [asg, show ¬ v < k by omega, show ¬ v < k + 1 by omega]

/-- **The value of a stack**: the truth of the matrix `φ` under the quantifiers of the prefix
bits `qs` from position `k` on, starting from the assignment of `S` at depth `k`. -/
def Val (qs : List Bool) (φ : CNF ℕ) (k S : ℕ) : Prop :=
  QBF.truthAux φ ((qs.drop k).map QBF.quantOfBit) (asg k S) k

/-- At the full depth the value is the matrix's value. -/
theorem val_leaf (qs : List Bool) (φ : CNF ℕ) (S : ℕ) :
    Val qs φ qs.length S ↔ φ.eval (asg qs.length S) = true := by
  simp [Val, QBF.truthAux]

/-- The prefix bits from position `k < |qs|` on. -/
private theorem drop_map_eq (qs : List Bool) (k : ℕ) (hk : k < qs.length) :
    (qs.drop k).map QBF.quantOfBit =
      QBF.quantOfBit qs[k] :: (qs.drop (k + 1)).map QBF.quantOfBit := by
  rw [List.drop_eq_getElem_cons hk, List.map_cons]

/-- **An existential level**: the value is the disjunction of the two pushes. -/
theorem val_ex (qs : List Bool) (φ : CNF ℕ) (k S : ℕ) (hk : k < qs.length)
    (hq : qs[k] = true) :
    Val qs φ k S ↔ Val qs φ (k + 1) (2 * S) ∨ Val qs φ (k + 1) (2 * S + 1) := by
  unfold Val
  rw [drop_map_eq qs k hk, hq]
  simp only [QBF.quantOfBit, if_true, QBF.truthAux, asg_push]
  constructor
  · rintro ⟨b, hb⟩; cases b
    · left; simpa using hb
    · right; simpa using hb
  · rintro (h | h)
    · exact ⟨false, by simpa using h⟩
    · exact ⟨true, by simpa using h⟩

/-- **A universal level**: the value is the conjunction of the two pushes. -/
theorem val_all (qs : List Bool) (φ : CNF ℕ) (k S : ℕ) (hk : k < qs.length)
    (hq : qs[k] = false) :
    Val qs φ k S ↔ Val qs φ (k + 1) (2 * S) ∧ Val qs φ (k + 1) (2 * S + 1) := by
  unfold Val
  rw [drop_map_eq qs k hk, hq]
  simp only [QBF.quantOfBit, Bool.false_eq_true, if_false, QBF.truthAux, asg_push]
  constructor
  · intro h; exact ⟨by simpa using h false, by simpa using h true⟩
  · rintro ⟨h0, h1⟩ b; cases b
    · simpa using h0
    · simpa using h1

/-- **The root**: the value of the stack `1` at depth `0` is the truth of the encoded formula. -/
theorem val_root (qs : List Bool) (φ : CNF ℕ) :
    Val qs φ 0 1 ↔ (QBF.decode (pairEncode qs (CNF.serialize φ))).truth := by
  rw [decode_pairEncode]
  simp [Val, QBF.truth, asg_zero]

end Complexity.LogProg.TQBFARM
```

## ===== TCSlib/Complexity/ClassPSPACE/TQBFARM/Walk.lean =====

```
/-
Copyright (c) 2026 TCSlib contributors. All rights reserved.
Released under Apache 2.0 license as described in the file LICENSE.
Authors: Hydroxyi
-/
import TCSlib.Complexity.ClassPSPACE.TQBFARM.Leaf

set_option maxHeartbeats 0
set_option relaxedAutoImplicit false
set_option autoImplicit false

/-!
# The syntax check and the assignment walk of the `TQBF` register machine

The `TQBF` register machine `Complexity.LogProg.TQBFARM.A` first runs the syntax automaton
over its input (`syn_run`), then evaluates the quantified formula by a depth-first walk over
the partial assignments of its prefix, kept as a binary stack `S` at depth `K`. This file
holds the walk's building blocks — locating a node's pair (`node_run`), pushing (`push_run`),
popping (`pop_run`), the quantifier lookup (`qlook_run`) — and its correctness at a leaf
(`leaf_spec`), where the matrix is evaluated (`Complexity.LogProg.TQBFARM.formula_run`).
The inner nodes and the conclusion `TQBF ∈ PSPACE` are in
`TCSlib.Complexity.ClassPSPACE.TQBFARM.Correct`.

Infrastructure for [AB09, §4.2, Theorem 4.13, membership half]; not itself a result of the
book.

## Main definitions

* `Complexity.LogProg.TQBFARM.stp` — the register files of the walk.
* `Complexity.LogProg.TQBFARM.CallOK` — the correctness of the walk at a depth.

## Main results

* `Complexity.LogProg.TQBFARM.syn_run` — the syntax check.
* `Complexity.LogProg.TQBFARM.node_run`, `push_run`, `pop_run`, `qlook_run` — the walk's
  steps.
* `Complexity.LogProg.TQBFARM.leaf_spec` — the walk is correct at a leaf.

## References

* [AB09] S. Arora, B. Barak, *Computational Complexity: A Modern Approach*,
  Cambridge University Press, 2009. (§4.2, Theorem 4.13.)
-/

namespace Complexity.LogProg

namespace TQBFARM

open Turing
open Std.Sat (CNF)

variable {x : List Bool} {B : ℕ}

/-! ## The syntax check -/

/-- **A length query answered `1`**. -/
lemma len_t {l l₁ l₀ : Lb} {st : St} {c : AConf 7 Lb}
    (hl : A l = .call 1 .whole [rP] l₁ l₀) (hbd : st.Bd B) (hp : st.P < x.length)
    (h : AReach A orc x (GuardLe A x B) (some l₁, st.toV, none) c) :
    AReach A orc x (GuardLe A x B) (some l, st.toV, none) c := by
  refine step_of hbd ?_
  simp only [astep, hl, vword_whole₁]
  rw [St.toV_P, orc_len, decide_eq_true hp, if_pos rfl]
  exact h

/-- **A length query answered `0`**. -/
lemma len_f {l l₁ l₀ : Lb} {st : St} {c : AConf 7 Lb}
    (hl : A l = .call 1 .whole [rP] l₁ l₀) (hbd : st.Bd B) (hp : ¬ st.P < x.length)
    (h : AReach A orc x (GuardLe A x B) (some l₀, st.toV, none) c) :
    AReach A orc x (GuardLe A x B) (some l, st.toV, none) c := by
  refine step_of hbd ?_
  simp only [astep, hl, vword_whole₁]
  rw [St.toV_P, orc_len, decide_eq_false hp, if_neg (by decide)]
  exact h

/-- **The syntax loop**: from `vl q` at `P = |x| - n`, the machine steps the automaton over the
rest of the input and reaches `vend q'` at `P = |x|`.

**Proof sketch.** Induction on `n`: below the end, the length query succeeds, the bit is read
and the automaton stepped; at the end the query fails. -/
theorem syn_run : ∀ (n : ℕ) (q : SynSt) (st : St), st.P + n = x.length → st.Bd B →
    x.length ≤ B →
    Run x B (.vl q) st (.vend ((x.drop st.P).foldl synStep q)) { st with P := x.length } := by
  intro n
  induction n with
  | zero =>
    intro q st hn hbd hx
    refine len_f (l := .vl q) rfl hbd (by omega) ?_
    rw [List.drop_eq_nil_of_le (by omega), List.foldl_nil]
    exact fin_of (by sext)
  | succ n ih =>
    intro q st hn hbd hx
    have hlt : st.P < x.length := by omega
    have hd : x.drop st.P = x[st.P] :: x.drop (st.P + 1) := List.drop_eq_getElem_cons hlt
    generalize x[st.P] = b at hd
    have hbd1 : St.Bd B { st with P := st.P + 1 } := by bdt
    have := ih (synStep q b) { st with P := st.P + 1 } (by simp; omega) hbd1 hx
    refine len_t (l := .vl q) rfl hbd hlt ?_
    refine read_b (l := .vr q) rfl hbd (getD_of_drop hd) ?_
    rw [hd, List.foldl_cons]
    cases b <;>
    · refine step_of hbd ?_
      regs [astep, A, cond_true, cond_false]
      exact this

/-! ## The walk -/

/-- **The register file of the walk** at depth `k`, with stack `S` and pointer `p`: every
other register clear. -/
def stp (k S p : ℕ) : St := ⟨k, S, p, 0, 0, 0, 0⟩

/-- Continue a run from an equal register file. -/
lemma cont {st st' : St} {l : Lb} {c : AConf 7 Lb} (e : st = st')
    (h : AReach A orc x (GuardLe A x B) (some l, st'.toV, none) c) :
    AReach A orc x (GuardLe A x B) (some l, st.toV, none) c := e ▸ h

/-- A walk register file is bounded. -/
lemma stp_bd {k S p : ℕ} (hk : k ≤ B) (hS : S ≤ B) (hp : p ≤ B) : (stp k S p).Bd B := by
  simp only [St.Bd, stp]; omega

section Walk

variable {qs : List Bool} {φ : CNF ℕ}

/-- The bits of an encoded formula: the doubled prefix, then the separator `01`. -/
lemma getD_enc (hx : x = pairEncode qs (CNF.serialize φ)) (j : ℕ) :
    x.getD j false = if j < 2 * qs.length then qs.getD (j / 2) false
      else if j = 2 * qs.length then false
      else if j = 2 * qs.length + 1 then true
      else (CNF.serialize φ).getD (j - 2 * qs.length - 2) false := by
  rw [hx, pairEncode_getD]

/-- The length of an encoded formula: at least `2|qs| + 2`. -/
lemma length_enc (hx : x = pairEncode qs (CNF.serialize φ)) : 2 * qs.length + 2 ≤ x.length := by
  rw [hx, length_pairEncode]; omega

/-- **Locating the node's pair**: from `node`, the machine sets `P := 2K` and reaches `nd1`. -/
theorem node_run (k S p : ℕ) (hk : 2 * k ≤ B) (hS : S ≤ B) (hp : p ≤ B) :
    Run x B .node (stp k S p) .nd1 (stp k S (2 * k)) := by
  refine step_of (stp_bd (by omega) hS hp) ?_
  regs [astep, A]
  refine cont (st' := stp k S 0) rfl ?_
  refine (cp_run .ndA _ (stp_bd (by omega) hS (by omega)) rfl
    (by simp only [cpDst, cpSrc]; regs; simp [stp]; omega)).trans ?_
  regs [cpDst, cpSrc, cpExit]
  refine cont (st' := stp k S k) (by sext [stp]) ?_
  refine (cp_run .ndB _ (stp_bd (by omega) hS (by omega)) rfl
    (by simp only [cpDst, cpSrc]; regs; simp [stp]; omega)).trans ?_
  regs [cpDst, cpSrc, cpExit]
  exact fin_of (by sext [stp])

/-- **A push**: from `push b` at depth `k` with stack `S` (any pointer), the machine reaches
`node` at depth `k + 1` with stack `2S + b`.

**Proof sketch.** Straight-line code: clear `P`; the doubled move (`dm_run`) gives `T = 2S`,
`S = 0`; the move back (`mv_run`) gives `S = 2S`, `T = 0`; for `b = 1` increment `S`; then
increment `K`. Each step keeps the registers below `B` (`stp_bd`). -/
theorem push_run (b : Bool) (k S p : ℕ) (hp : p ≤ B) (hS : 2 * S + 1 ≤ B) (hk : k + 1 ≤ B) :
    Run x B (.push b) (stp k S p) .node (stp (k + 1) (2 * S + b.toNat) 0) := by
  refine step_of (stp_bd (by omega) (by omega) hp) ?_
  regs [astep, A]
  refine cont (st' := stp k S 0) rfl ?_
  refine (dm_run b _ (stp_bd (by omega) (by omega) (by omega)) (by simp [stp]; omega)).trans ?_
  refine cont (st' := ⟨k, 0, 0, 2 * S, 0, 0, 0⟩) (by sext [stp]) ?_
  refine (mv_run b _ (by simp only [St.Bd]; omega) (by simp; omega)).trans ?_
  refine cont (st' := ⟨k, 2 * S, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0⟩) (by sext) ?_
  cases b
  · simp only [Bool.false_eq_true, if_false]
    refine step_of (by simp only [St.Bd]; omega) ?_
    regs [astep, A]
    exact fin_of (by sext [stp])
  · simp only [if_true]
    refine step_of (by simp only [St.Bd]; omega) ?_
    regs [astep, A]
    refine step_of (by simp only [St.Bd]; omega) ?_
    regs [astep, A]
    exact fin_of (by sext [stp])

/-- **A pop**: from `rt v` at depth `k + 1` with stack `2S + b`, the machine returns to depth
`k` with stack `S`, at `rt v` after a second child (`b = 1`) and at the quantifier lookup after
a first child.

**Proof sketch.** Straight-line code: `K = k + 1 ≠ 0`, so `rt v` decrements `K`; the parity
test of `S = 2S + b` branches on `b`, and both branches halve `S` (`(2S + b) / 2 = S`), going
on to `rt v` (`b = 1`) or to the quantifier lookup (`b = 0`). -/
theorem pop_run (v b : Bool) (k S : ℕ) (hk : k + 1 ≤ B) (hS : 2 * S + 1 ≤ B) :
    Run x B (.rt v) (stp (k + 1) (2 * S + b.toNat) 0) (cond b (.rt v) (.cp (.qA v) 0))
      (stp k S 0) := by
  have hb : b.toNat ≤ 1 := Bool.toNat_le b
  refine step_of (stp_bd hk (by omega) (by omega)) ?_
  regs [astep, A]
  simp only [stp, Nat.add_one_ne_zero, if_false]
  refine step_of (stp_bd hk (by omega) (by omega)) ?_
  regs [astep, A]
  refine cont (st' := stp k (2 * S + b.toNat) 0) (by sext [stp]) ?_
  refine step_of (stp_bd (by omega) (by omega) (by omega)) ?_
  regs [astep, A]
  have h2 : (2 * S + b.toNat) / 2 = S := by omega
  cases b
  · simp only [stp, Bool.toNat_false, add_zero, Nat.mul_mod_right, zero_ne_one, if_false]
    refine step_of (stp_bd (B := B) (k := k) (S := 2 * S) (p := 0) (by omega) (by omega)
      (by omega)) ?_
    regs [astep, A]
    exact fin_of (by sext [stp])
  · simp only [stp, Bool.toNat_true, Nat.mul_add_mod, Nat.one_mod, if_true]
    refine step_of (stp_bd (B := B) (k := k) (S := 2 * S + 1) (p := 0) (by omega) (by omega)
      (by omega)) ?_
    regs [astep, A]
    exact fin_of (by sext [stp])

/-- **The quantifier lookup**: from `cp (qA v) 0` at depth `k`, the machine sets `P := 2K` and
reaches `qr v`. -/
theorem qlook_run (v : Bool) (k S : ℕ) (hk : 2 * k ≤ B) (hS : S ≤ B) :
    Run x B (.cp (.qA v) 0) (stp k S 0) (.qr v) (stp k S (2 * k)) := by
  refine (cp_run (.qA v) _ (stp_bd (by omega) hS (by omega)) rfl
    (by simp only [cpDst, cpSrc]; regs; simp [stp]; omega)).trans ?_
  regs [cpDst, cpSrc, cpExit]
  refine cont (st' := stp k S k) (by sext [stp]) ?_
  refine (cp_run (.qB v) _ (stp_bd (by omega) hS (by omega)) rfl
    (by simp only [cpDst, cpSrc]; regs; simp [stp]; omega)).trans ?_
  regs [cpDst, cpSrc, cpExit]
  exact fin_of (by sext [stp])

variable (x B qs φ) in
open Classical in
/-- **The walk is correct at depth `k`**: from `node` at depth `k` with any stack `S` below
`2 ^ (k + 1)`, the machine reaches `rt v` with the same registers, `v` the value
`Val qs φ k S`. -/
def CallOK (k : ℕ) : Prop :=
  ∀ S, S < 2 ^ (k + 1) →
    Run x B .node (stp k S 0) (.rt (decide (Val qs φ k S))) (stp k S 0)

open Classical in
/-- **A leaf**: at depth `|qs|` the walk returns the value of the matrix.

**Proof sketch.** The pair at `2K` is the separator: bit `2K` is `0`, bit `2K + 1` is `1`;
the matrix starts at `2K + 2` (`formula_run`), and `val_leaf` identifies its value. -/
theorem leaf_spec (hx : x = pairEncode qs (CNF.serialize φ)) (hB1 : 2 ^ (qs.length + 1) ≤ B)
    (hB2 : x.length ≤ B) : CallOK x B qs φ qs.length := by
  intro S hS
  have hlen := length_enc hx
  set M := qs.length with hM
  refine (node_run M S 0 (by omega) (by omega) (by omega)).trans ?_
  refine read_f (l := .nd1) rfl (stp_bd (by omega) (by omega) (by omega))
    (by show x.getD (2 * M) false = false; rw [getD_enc hx, ← hM]; simp) ?_
  refine step_of (stp_bd (by omega) (by omega) (by omega)) ?_
  regs [astep, A]
  refine cont (st' := stp M S (2 * M + 1)) rfl ?_
  refine read_t (l := .nd3) rfl (stp_bd (by omega) (by omega) (by omega))
    (by show x.getD (2 * M + 1) false = true; rw [getD_enc hx, ← hM]; simp) ?_
  refine step_of (stp_bd (by omega) (by omega) (by omega)) ?_
  regs [astep, A]
  refine cont (st' := stp M S (2 * M + 2)) rfl ?_
  have hd : x.drop (stp M S (2 * M + 2)).P = CNF.serialize φ ++ [] := by
    rw [hx]; simp [stp, pairEncode_eq_dbl, List.drop_append, hM]
  have := formula_run [] φ (stp M S (2 * M + 2)) hd (stp_bd (by omega) (by omega) (by omega))
    hB2 rfl rfl rfl rfl
  have hv : decide (Val qs φ M S) = CNF.eval (asg M S) φ := by
    rw [hM, Bool.eq_iff_iff, decide_eq_true_iff, val_leaf]
  rw [hv]
  exact reach_of_eq this (by congr 3)

end Walk

end TQBFARM

end Complexity.LogProg
```

## ===== TCSlib/Complexity/ClassPSPACE/TQBFHard.lean =====

```
/-
Copyright (c) 2026 TCSlib contributors. All rights reserved.
Released under Apache 2.0 license as described in the file LICENSE.
Authors: Hydroxyi
-/
import TCSlib.Complexity.ClassPSPACE.TQBFHardParams
import TCSlib.Complexity.ClassPSPACE.TQBFHardTseitin
import TCSlib.Complexity.CircuitComplexity.UniformTableau
import TCSlib.Complexity.CircuitComplexity.CircuitSatReduction
import TCSlib.Complexity.SpaceComplexity.SpaceClasses
import TCSlib.Complexity.ClassNP.Reductions

set_option maxHeartbeats 0
set_option relaxedAutoImplicit false
set_option autoImplicit false

/-!
# `TQBF` is `PSPACE`-hard

[AB09, Theorem 4.13, hardness half]: every language in `PSPACE` reduces in polynomial time to
the true quantified Boolean formulas. Let `N` decide `L` in nondeterministic space
`d (n^c + 1)` (`Complexity.PSPACE_subset_NPSPACE`). On input `x` of length `n` the reduction
outputs the encoding of a closed formula

`∃ Z₀ A B ∃ Z_w ∀ U_w ∀ V_w ⋯ ∃ Z₁ ∀ U₁ ∀ V₁ ∃ (auxiliary) · matrix`

over blocks of `w = wCoef N d · (n + 1)^(c + 1)` variables, `w` levels deep:

* **the `ψᵢ` recursion** ([AB09]'s `∀`-folding, `TQBFHardSemantics`): truth of the prefix of
  the levels is the midpoint recursion over the one-step relation of blocks, i.e. a path of
  `2^w` steps (`Complexity.TQBFHard.prefixTruth_top`, `Complexity.TQBFHard.mid_iff_steps`);
* **the configuration graph** (`TQBFHardMachine`): blocks carry code words of the
  configuration codec `Complexity.Codec`, and an initial block reaches an accepting block in
  `2^w` steps iff `x ∈ L` (`Complexity.TQBFHard.mem_iff_mid`; `2^w` bounds the vertex count,
  `Complexity.TQBFHard.configBound_le_two_pow`);
* **the matrix** is the predicate "the block at `w` is initial, the block at `2w` is
  accepting, and the selection chain of the levels ends in a step", computed by the
  polynomial-time verifier `Complexity.TQBFHard.predB` (`TQBFHardVerifier`,
  `TQBFHardBridge`), written as a circuit — the uniform configuration tableau
  `Complexity.cfgTab` of a machine computing the verifier, with `⟨x, ·⟩` hard-wired — and
  turned into a CNF by Tseitin's transformation `BoolCircuit.DAGCircuit.toCNF`, whose gate
  variables are quantified existentially after the whole prefix
  (`Complexity.QBF.truth_exSuffix_of_pointwise` with `Complexity.TQBFHard.toCNF_extension_iff`).

**Polynomial time.** The reduction is a composition of polynomial-time maps: the unary input
`1^{3w(w+1)} 0 1^T 0 ⟨x, ⟩` of the tableau emitter (`Complexity.polyTimeComputable_tabInput`),
the emitter itself (`Complexity.UTab.polyTimeComputable_tabEmit`, [AB09, Remark 6.7]), the
CKT-SAT-to-SAT map (`BoolCircuit.polyTimeComputable_dagCktSatToSAT3`, [AB09, Lemma 6.11]),
and the prefix bits (`Complexity.TQBFHard.polyTimeComputable_levelBits`).

**Deviation from the book's route.** [AB09] writes `ψ₀` as a CNF for the adjacency of two
configurations (Claim 4.4(2)) and leaves the reduction's running time to the reader. Here the
matrix of the whole prenex formula is one polynomial-time predicate, made a CNF by the
P-uniform tableau and Tseitin, so that no configuration-specific CNF (and no emitter for one)
is needed; the configuration codec `Complexity.ConfigCodec` of `ClassPSPACE.TQBF` is not
used. The midpoints quantify over all blocks without a validity guard: the one-step
relation of blocks is "equal, or a step pair of codes", and a step pair's target is always a
code word, so junk midpoints only occur on trivial (equality) paths.

## Main definitions

* `Complexity.TQBFHard.redQuants`, `Complexity.TQBFHard.redCircuit`,
  `Complexity.TQBFHard.redQBF`, `Complexity.TQBFHard.redMap` — the reduction.

## Main results

* `Complexity.TQBFHard.truth_redQBF` — the formula is true iff `x ∈ L`.
* `Complexity.TQBFHard.polyTimeComputable_redMap` — the reduction is polynomial-time.
* `Complexity.TQBFHard.PSPACE_polyTimeReducible_TQBF` — `L ∈ PSPACE` reduces to the true
  quantified Boolean formulas. [AB09, Theorem 4.13, hardness half]

## References

* [AB09] S. Arora, B. Barak, *Computational Complexity: A Modern Approach*,
  Cambridge University Press, 2009. (§4.2, Theorem 4.13 and its proof; §6.1, Remark 6.7 and
  Lemma 6.11.)
* [SM73] L. Stockmeyer, A. Meyer, *Word problems requiring exponential time*, STOC 1973.
  (Cited through [AB09].)
-/

namespace Complexity

namespace TQBFHard

open Turing BoolCircuit Codec QBF Std.Sat

/-- **The CKT-SAT reduction map on a description** of a fan-in-two circuit is the
serialization of its Tseitin formula. -/
theorem dagCktSatToSAT3_encode {n : ℕ} (C : DAGCircuit n) (hC : C.IsFaninTwo) :
    dagCktSatToSAT3 C.encode = CNF.serialize C.toCNF := by
  simp [dagCktSatToSAT3, dagCktSatToCNF, DAGCircuit.decode_encode, hC]

variable (N : FinNDTM Bool) (d c : ℕ) (V : FinTM Bool) (CV cV : ℕ)

/-- The block width `w = wCoef N d · (n + 1)^(c + 1)`. -/
def redW (n : ℕ) : ℕ := vwid (wCoef N d) (c + 1) n

/-- The number `3w(w + 1)` of prefix variables. -/
def redM (n : ℕ) : ℕ := 3 * redW N d c n * redW N d c n + 3 * redW N d c n

/-- The constant bounding `|⟨x, σ⟩| + 1` by `K (n + 1)^(2(c + 1))`. -/
def redK : ℕ := 3 * wCoef N d * wCoef N d + 3 * wCoef N d + 3

/-- The tableau's time bound: at least the verifier's running time on `⟨x, σ⟩`, and `≥ 1`. -/
def redT (n : ℕ) : ℕ := CV * redK N d ^ cV * (n + 1) ^ (2 * (c + 1) * cV) + 1

/-- **The matrix circuit**: the uniform tableau of the verifier machine `V` for
`redT n` steps, on `3w(w + 1)` free inputs (the prefix variables) after the hard-wired word
`⟨x, ` (`pairEncode x []`). -/
noncomputable def redCircuit (x : List Bool) : DAGCircuit (redM N d c x.length) :=
  cfgTab V (redM N d c x.length) (pairEncode x []) (redT N d c CV cV x.length)

/-- **The quantifier prefix**: three existential blocks (the pad `Z₀`, the source `A`, the
target `B`), then `w` levels `∃^w ∀^w ∀^w`. -/
def redQuants (n : ℕ) : List Quant :=
  List.replicate (redW N d c n) .ex ++ (List.replicate (redW N d c n) .ex ++
    (List.replicate (redW N d c n) .ex ++ levelQuants (redW N d c n) (redW N d c n)))

/-- **The quantified formula**: the prefix, then one existential per letter of the
serialized matrix (enough for every Tseitin variable), and the Tseitin formula of the matrix
circuit. -/
noncomputable def redQBF (x : List Bool) : QBF :=
  ⟨redQuants N d c x.length ++
      List.replicate (CNF.serialize (redCircuit N d c V CV cV x).toCNF).length .ex,
    (redCircuit N d c V CV cV x).toCNF⟩

/-- **The reduction map**: the encoding of `redQBF x`. -/
noncomputable def redMap (x : List Bool) : List Bool := QBF.encode (redQBF N d c V CV cV x)

/-- The prefix has `3w(w + 1)` variables. -/
theorem length_redQuants (n : ℕ) : (redQuants N d c n).length = redM N d c n := by
  simp only [redQuants, List.length_append, List.length_replicate, length_levelQuants, redM]
  ring

/-- **The verifier runs within the tableau's time bound** on `⟨x, σ⟩`, `|σ| = 3w(w + 1)`.

**Proof sketch.** With `P = (n + 1) ^ (c + 1)` and `A = wCoef N d`, the input length is
`|⟨x, σ⟩| + 1 = 2n + 3 + 3A²P² + 3AP ≤ redK · P² = redK · (n + 1) ^ (2(c + 1))` (using
`n + 1 ≤ P ≤ P²`); raising to `cV` and multiplying by `CV` gives
`CV · redK ^ cV · (n + 1) ^ (2(c + 1) cV) ≤ redT`. -/
theorem time_le (x σ : List Bool) (hσ : σ.length = redM N d c x.length) :
    CV * ((pairEncode x σ).length + 1) ^ cV ≤ redT N d c CV cV x.length := by
  set n := x.length
  set A := wCoef N d
  set P := (n + 1) ^ (c + 1)
  have hP1 : 1 ≤ P := Nat.one_le_pow _ _ (by omega)
  have hnP : n + 1 ≤ P := by
    calc n + 1 = (n + 1) ^ 1 := (pow_one _).symm
      _ ≤ P := Nat.pow_le_pow_right (by omega) (by omega)
  have hPP : P ≤ P * P := Nat.le_mul_of_pos_right _ hP1
  have hlen : (pairEncode x σ).length + 1 ≤ redK N d * (n + 1) ^ (2 * (c + 1)) := by
    rw [length_pairEncode, hσ]
    have e1 : (n + 1) ^ (2 * (c + 1)) = P * P := by rw [two_mul, pow_add]
    have e2 : redM N d c n = 3 * A * A * (P * P) + 3 * A * P := by
      simp only [redM, redW, vwid, A, P]; ring
    rw [e1, e2]
    have h1 : 3 * A * P ≤ 3 * A * (P * P) := Nat.mul_le_mul_left _ hPP
    have h2 : 2 * n + 3 ≤ 3 * (P * P) := by nlinarith
    have e3 : redK N d * (P * P) = 3 * A * A * (P * P) + 3 * A * (P * P) + 3 * (P * P) := by
      simp only [redK, A]; ring
    rw [e3]
    omega
  calc CV * ((pairEncode x σ).length + 1) ^ cV
      ≤ CV * (redK N d * (n + 1) ^ (2 * (c + 1))) ^ cV :=
        Nat.mul_le_mul_left _ (Nat.pow_le_pow_left hlen _)
    _ = CV * redK N d ^ cV * (n + 1) ^ (2 * (c + 1) * cV) := by rw [mul_pow, ← pow_mul]; ring
    _ ≤ redT N d c CV cV n := Nat.le_succ _

/-- **The matrix circuit computes the verifier** on `⟨x, σ⟩`, `σ` its input assignment.

**Proof sketch.** `Complexity.cfgTab_eval`: the tableau outputs `1` iff `V` emits `1` within
`redT` steps on `⟨x, ⟩ ++ σ = ⟨x, σ⟩`; `V` computes `[predB ⟨x, σ⟩]` within that time
(`time_le`), so this is `predB ⟨x, σ⟩` (`Complexity.decide_emits_eq_of_computesInTime`). -/
theorem eval_redCircuit
    (hV : V.ComputesFunInTime (fun y => [predB N d c (wCoef N d) (c + 1) y])
      (fun m => CV * (m + 1) ^ cV))
    (x : List Bool) (τ : ℕ → Bool) :
    (redCircuit N d c V CV cV x).eval (fun i => τ i) =
      predB N d c (wCoef N d) (c + 1)
        (pairEncode x (List.ofFn fun j : Fin (redM N d c x.length) => τ j)) := by
  set σ := List.ofFn fun j : Fin (redM N d c x.length) => τ j
  have hσ : σ.length = redM N d c x.length := by simp [σ]
  have hz : pairEncode x [] ++ σ = pairEncode x σ := by
    simp [pairEncode, List.append_assoc]
  rw [redCircuit, cfgTab_eval, hz]
  exact decide_emits_eq_of_computesInTime
    ((hV (pairEncode x σ)).mono (time_le N d c CV cV x σ hσ))

variable {N d c}

/-- **The formula is true iff `x ∈ L`** ([AB09, Theorem 4.13, the proof]): for `N` deciding
`L` in space `d (n^c + 1)` and `V` computing the verifier in time `CV (m + 1)^{cV}`.

**Proof sketch.** Tseitin after the prefix (`Complexity.QBF.truth_exSuffix_of_pointwise`,
`toCNF_extension_iff`; the serialization is longer than the number of variables,
`numVars_le_length_serialize`) leaves the prefix truth of "the circuit accepts the prefix
assignment", which is the verifier (`eval_redCircuit`), i.e. the initial and accepting tests
and the flat matrix (`predB_iff`), i.e. the prenex `ψ` matrix (`levelMatrix_iff_flat`). Its
prefix truth is "some initial `A` reaches some accepting `B` in the midpoint recursion of
depth `w`" (`prefixTruth_top`), which is `x ∈ L` (`mem_iff_mid`, with the radius at least the
space bound and the width bounds `vlen_le_vwid`, `configBound_le_two_pow`). -/
theorem truth_redQBF {L : Language Bool} (hN : N.DecidesInSpace L fun n => d * (n ^ c + 1))
    (hV : V.ComputesFunInTime (fun y => [predB N d c (wCoef N d) (c + 1) y])
      (fun m => CV * (m + 1) ^ cV))
    (x : List Bool) : (redQBF N d c V CV cV x).truth ↔ x ∈ L := by
  set n := x.length
  set w := redW N d c n with hw
  set s := vrad d c n
  set Lc := vlen N d c n
  set C := redCircuit N d c V CV cV x
  have hqlen := length_redQuants N d c n
  -- Tseitin after the prefix
  rw [redQBF, truth_exSuffix_of_pointwise (redQuants N d c n) C.toCNF _
    (fun σ => C.eval (fun i => σ i) = true)
    ((numVars_le_length_serialize _).trans (Nat.le_add_left _ _))
    (fun σ => by rw [hqlen]; exact toCNF_extension_iff C (cfgTab_isFaninTwo _ _ _ _).2 σ)]
  -- the circuit is the prenex matrix
  have hleaf : ∀ τ : ℕ → Bool, C.eval (fun i => τ i) = true ↔
      blockInit N x s Lc (readBlock τ w w) ∧ blockAcc N x s Lc (readBlock τ (2 * w) w) ∧
        levelMatrix w (blockStep N x s Lc) w (3 * w) (readBlock τ w w)
          (readBlock τ (2 * w) w) τ := by
    intro τ
    rw [eval_redCircuit N d c V CV cV hV x τ]
    have hflat := levelMatrix_iff_flat w (blockStep N x s Lc) τ w 0
    simp only [Nat.zero_add, Nat.mul_one, uRec, vRec, Nat.mul_zero] at hflat
    rw [hflat]
    exact predB_iff N d c (wCoef N d) (c + 1) x τ (vlen_le_vwid N d c n)
  rw [prefixTruth_congr hleaf]
  rw [redQuants, prefixTruth_top]
  have hs : d * (n ^ c + 1) ≤ s := by
    have h1 : n ^ c ≤ (n + 1) ^ c := Nat.pow_le_pow_left (by omega) _
    have h2 : 1 ≤ (n + 1) ^ c := Nat.one_le_pow _ _ (by omega)
    have : d * (n ^ c + 1) ≤ d * (2 * (n + 1) ^ c) := Nat.mul_le_mul_left _ (by omega)
    simp only [s, vrad]
    linarith
  exact (mem_iff_mid N hN x s w hs (vlen_le_vwid N d c n) (configBound_le_two_pow N d c n)).symm

variable (N d c)

/-- The unary number of prefix variables is polynomial-time. -/
theorem pt_redM : PolyTimeComputable fun x => List.replicate (redM N d c x.length) true := by
  have h := (polyTimeComputable_polyUnary (3 * wCoef N d * wCoef N d) (2 * (c + 1))).append
    (polyTimeComputable_polyUnary (3 * wCoef N d) (c + 1))
  convert h using 1
  funext x
  rw [← List.replicate_add]
  congr 1
  simp only [redM, redW, vwid, two_mul, pow_add]
  ring

/-- **The reduction is polynomial-time** ([AB09, Theorem 4.13]: "the formula can be computed
in polynomial time").

**Proof sketch.** `redMap x` is the pair of the prefix bits and the serialized Tseitin
formula. The formula is the CKT-SAT map (`BoolCircuit.polyTimeComputable_dagCktSatToSAT3`)
of the tableau emitter's output (`Complexity.UTab.polyTimeComputable_tabEmit`,
`Complexity.UTab.tabEmit_eq`) on the polynomial-time input `1^M 0 1^T 0 ⟨x, ⟩`
(`Complexity.polyTimeComputable_tabInput`); the prefix bits are `1^{3w}`, the level bits
(`polyTimeComputable_levelBits`), and one `1` per letter of the formula. -/
theorem polyTimeComputable_redMap : PolyTimeComputable (redMap N d c V CV cV) := by
  have hT : PolyTimeComputable fun x =>
      List.replicate (redT N d c CV cV x.length) true := by
    have := (polyTimeComputable_polyUnary (CV * redK N d ^ cV) (2 * (c + 1) * cV)).append
      (polyTimeComputable_const [true])
    convert this using 1
    funext x
    simp [redT, List.replicate_add]
  have hinp := polyTimeComputable_tabInput (pt_redM N d c) hT
    (polyTimeComputable_id.pairEncode (polyTimeComputable_const []))
  have hser := polyTimeComputable_dagCktSatToSAT3.comp
    ((UTab.polyTimeComputable_tabEmit V).comp hinp)
  have hser_eq : ∀ x, (dagCktSatToSAT3 ∘ UTab.tabEmit V ∘ fun x =>
      List.replicate (redM N d c x.length) true ++ false ::
        (List.replicate (redT N d c CV cV x.length) true ++ false :: pairEncode (id x) [])) x =
      CNF.serialize (redCircuit N d c V CV cV x).toCNF := by
    intro x
    simp only [Function.comp, id]
    rw [UTab.tabEmit_eq V _ _ _ (by simp [redT]), dagCktSatToSAT3_encode _
      (cfgTab_isFaninTwo _ _ _ _)]
    rfl
  have h3w : PolyTimeComputable fun x =>
      List.replicate (3 * redW N d c x.length) true := by
    have := polyTimeComputable_polyUnary (3 * wCoef N d) (c + 1)
    convert this using 1
    funext x
    simp only [redW, vwid]
    ring_nf
  have hlev := polyTimeComputable_levelBits (w := fun x => redW N d c x.length)
    (polyTimeComputable_polyUnary (wCoef N d) (c + 1))
  have hall := ((h3w.append hlev).append (polyTimeComputable_unary.comp hser)).pairEncode hser
  convert hall using 1
  funext x
  have hs : dagCktSatToSAT3 (UTab.tabEmit V (List.replicate (redM N d c x.length) true ++
      false :: (List.replicate (redT N d c CV cV x.length) true ++ false :: pairEncode x []))) =
      CNF.serialize (redCircuit N d c V CV cV x).toCNF := by
    simpa using hser_eq x
  simp only [Function.comp, id, hs]
  simp only [redMap, QBF.encode, redQBF, redQuants, List.map_append, List.map_replicate,
    map_quantBit_levelQuants, quantBit]
  congr 1
  rw [show 3 * redW N d c x.length =
      redW N d c x.length + redW N d c x.length + redW N d c x.length by ring,
    List.replicate_add, List.replicate_add]
  simp only [List.append_assoc]

/-- **`PSPACE` reduces to `TQBF`** ([AB09, Theorem 4.13, hardness half]): every language in
`PSPACE` Karp-reduces in polynomial time to the set of strings whose decoded quantified
Boolean formula is true.

**Proof sketch.** `L ∈ NPSPACE` (`Complexity.PSPACE_subset_NPSPACE`): some `N` decides `L` in
space `d (n^c + 1)`. The verifier of the reduction is polynomial-time
(`polyTimeComputable_predB`); take a machine `V` computing it. The map `redMap` is
polynomial-time (`polyTimeComputable_redMap`) and decodes to `redQBF x`
(`Complexity.QBF.decode_encode`), which is true iff `x ∈ L` (`truth_redQBF`). -/
theorem PSPACE_polyTimeReducible_TQBF {L : Language Bool} (hL : L ∈ PSPACE) :
    L ≤ₚ {x | (QBF.decode x).truth} := by
  obtain ⟨c, hc⟩ := Set.mem_iUnion.mp (PSPACE_subset_NPSPACE hL)
  obtain ⟨d, N, hN⟩ := hc
  obtain ⟨V, CV, cV, hV⟩ := polyTimeComputable_predB N d c (wCoef N d) (c + 1)
  refine ⟨redMap N d c V CV cV, polyTimeComputable_redMap N d c V CV cV, fun x => ?_⟩
  show x ∈ L ↔ (QBF.decode (QBF.encode (redQBF N d c V CV cV x))).truth
  rw [QBF.decode_encode]
  exact (truth_redQBF V CV cV hN hV x).symm

end TQBFHard

end Complexity
```

## ===== TCSlib/Complexity/ClassPSPACE/TQBFHardBridge.lean =====

```
/-
Copyright (c) 2026 TCSlib contributors. All rights reserved.
Released under Apache 2.0 license as described in the file LICENSE.
Authors: Hydroxyi
-/
import TCSlib.Complexity.ClassPSPACE.TQBFHardVerifier

set_option maxHeartbeats 0
set_option relaxedAutoImplicit false
set_option autoImplicit false

/-!
# The verifier on an assignment

On the input `⟨x, σ⟩` with `σ` the first `3w(w + 1)` values of an assignment `τ` of the
prefix variables, the verifier `Complexity.TQBFHard.predB` of `TQBFHardVerifier` is the flat
form of the `ψ` matrix of `TQBFHardSemantics` over the block tests of `TQBFHardMachine`:
the initial-code test on the block at `w`, the accepting-code test on the block at `2w`, and
"some record's pair is not selected by its parent, or the innermost pair is one step"
(`predB_iff`). The proof reads every block of the word `σ` as the corresponding block of
`τ` (`ofFn_drop_take`).

Infrastructure for `Complexity.TQBF_PSPACEHard`; not itself a book result.

## Main results

* `Complexity.TQBFHard.predB_iff` — the verifier on an assignment.

## References

* [AB09] S. Arora, B. Barak, *Computational Complexity: A Modern Approach*,
  Cambridge University Press, 2009. (§4.2, Theorem 4.13.)
-/

namespace Complexity

namespace TQBFHard

open Turing Codec

/-- An indicator is `true` exactly on members. -/
theorem indicator_eq_true_iff {L : Language Bool} {z : List Bool} :
    MultiTapeTM.indicator L z = true ↔ z ∈ L := by
  unfold MultiTapeTM.indicator
  split_ifs with h <;> simp [h]

/-- A slice of the word of the first `M` values of `τ` is a block of `τ`. -/
theorem ofFn_drop_take (τ : ℕ → Bool) {M i k : ℕ} (h : i + k ≤ M) :
    ((List.ofFn fun j : Fin M => τ j).drop i).take k = readBlock τ i k := by
  apply List.ext_getElem
  · simp only [List.length_take, List.length_drop, List.length_ofFn, length_readBlock]
    omega
  · intro j h1 h2
    simp only [List.getElem_take, List.getElem_drop, List.getElem_ofFn, readBlock]

variable (N : FinNDTM Bool) (d c A a : ℕ)

/-- **The verifier on an assignment**: for an input `x` of length `n`, block width
`w = A (n + 1)^a` at least the code-word length `L`, radius `s = 2d (n + 1)^c`, and the word
`σ` of the first `3w(w + 1)` values of `τ`, the verifier accepts `⟨x, σ⟩` iff the block at `w`
is initial, the block at `2w` is accepting, and some record `j < w` has its successor's pair
not selected, or the pair of record `w` is one step.

**Proof sketch.** Each block the verifier cuts out of `σ` is the block of `τ` at the same
offset (`ofFn_drop_take`; the code-word prefix is the block's first `L` letters,
`List.take_take`), the window of record `j` holds the records `j` and `j + 1`, and the
indicators are memberships (`indicator_eq_true_iff`). -/
theorem predB_iff (x : List Bool) (τ : ℕ → Bool)
    (hL : vlen N d c x.length ≤ vwid A a x.length) :
    predB N d c A a (pairEncode x (List.ofFn fun j : Fin (3 * vwid A a x.length *
        vwid A a x.length + 3 * vwid A a x.length) => τ j)) = true ↔
      blockInit N x (vrad d c x.length) (vlen N d c x.length)
          (readBlock τ (vwid A a x.length) (vwid A a x.length)) ∧
        blockAcc N x (vrad d c x.length) (vlen N d c x.length)
          (readBlock τ (2 * vwid A a x.length) (vwid A a x.length)) ∧
        ((∃ i < vwid A a x.length, ¬ Sel (uRec τ (vwid A a x.length) i)
            (vRec τ (vwid A a x.length) i) (zRec τ (vwid A a x.length) (i + 1))
            (uRec τ (vwid A a x.length) (i + 1)) (vRec τ (vwid A a x.length) (i + 1))) ∨
          blockStep N x (vrad d c x.length) (vlen N d c x.length)
            (uRec τ (vwid A a x.length) (vwid A a x.length))
            (vRec τ (vwid A a x.length) (vwid A a x.length))) := by
  set w := vwid A a x.length with hw
  set L := vlen N d c x.length with hLdef
  set s := vrad d c x.length with hs
  set M := 3 * w * w + 3 * w with hM
  set σ := List.ofFn fun j : Fin M => τ j with hσ
  set y := pairEncode x σ with hy
  have hX : pairFstD y = x := by simp [hy]
  have hS : pairSndD y = σ := by simp [hy]
  -- blocks and code prefixes of `σ`
  have hblk : ∀ off, off + w ≤ M → blkAt A a y off = readBlock τ off w := by
    intro off hoff
    simp only [blkAt, hX, hS, ← hw]
    exact ofFn_drop_take τ hoff
  have hcp : ∀ off, off + w ≤ M → cpAt N d c y off = (readBlock τ off w).take L := by
    intro off hoff
    simp only [cpAt, hX, hS, ← hLdef]
    rw [← ofFn_drop_take τ hoff, List.take_take, Nat.min_eq_left hL]
  have hinit : initB N d c A a y = true ↔ blockInit N x s L (readBlock τ w w) := by
    simp only [initB, hX, ← hw, ← hs]
    rw [hcp w (by omega), indicator_eq_true_iff]
    rfl
  have hacc : accB N d c A a y = true ↔ blockAcc N x s L (readBlock τ (2 * w) w) := by
    simp only [accB, hX, ← hw, ← hs]
    rw [hcp (2 * w) (by omega), indicator_eq_true_iff]
    rfl
  have hbase : baseB N d c A a y = true ↔ blockStep N x s L (uRec τ w w) (vRec τ w w) := by
    simp only [baseB, hX, ← hw, ← hs]
    rw [hblk _ (by omega), hblk _ (by omega), hcp _ (by omega), hcp _ (by omega),
      Bool.or_eq_true, decide_eq_true_iff, indicator_eq_true_iff]
    rfl
  -- the windows
  have hwin : ∀ j < w, ∀ k ≤ 5, winBlk (lvlQ A a y j) k = readBlock τ (3 * w * j + k * w) w := by
    intro j hj k hk
    simp only [winBlk, lvlQ, hX, hS, ← hw, pairFstD_pairEncode, pairSndD_pairEncode,
      List.length_replicate, List.drop_drop]
    apply ofFn_drop_take τ
    have : (j + 2) * w ≤ (w + 1) * w := Nat.mul_le_mul_right _ (by omega)
    have : k * w ≤ 5 * w := Nat.mul_le_mul_right _ hk
    nlinarith
  have hsel : ∀ j < w, selT (lvlQ A a y j) = true ↔ Sel (uRec τ w j) (vRec τ w j)
      (zRec τ w (j + 1)) (uRec τ w (j + 1)) (vRec τ w (j + 1)) := by
    intro j hj
    simp only [selT, hwin j hj 1 (by omega), hwin j hj 2 (by omega), hwin j hj 3 (by omega),
      hwin j hj 4 (by omega), hwin j hj 5 (by omega), Bool.or_eq_true, Bool.and_eq_true,
      decide_eq_true_iff, Sel, uRec, vRec, zRec]
    have e3 : 3 * w * j + 3 * w = 3 * w * (j + 1) := by ring
    have e4 : 3 * w * j + 4 * w = 3 * w * (j + 1) + w := by ring
    have e5 : 3 * w * j + 5 * w = 3 * w * (j + 1) + 2 * w := by ring
    rw [Nat.one_mul, e3, e4, e5]
  have hor : orB A a y = true ↔ ∃ i < w, ¬ Sel (uRec τ w i) (vRec τ w i) (zRec τ w (i + 1))
      (uRec τ w (i + 1)) (vRec τ w (i + 1)) := by
    simp only [orB, hX, ← hw, List.any_eq_true, List.mem_range, Bool.not_eq_true']
    constructor
    · rintro ⟨j, hj, h⟩
      exact ⟨j, hj, fun hs' => by rw [← hsel j hj, h] at hs'; exact Bool.false_ne_true hs'⟩
    · rintro ⟨j, hj, h⟩
      refine ⟨j, hj, ?_⟩
      cases hb : selT (lvlQ A a y j)
      · rfl
      · exact absurd ((hsel j hj).mp hb) h
  simp only [predB, Bool.and_eq_true, Bool.or_eq_true]
  rw [hinit, hacc, hbase, hor, and_assoc]
  exact and_congr_right fun _ => and_congr_right fun _ => or_comm

end TQBFHard

end Complexity
```

## ===== TCSlib/Complexity/ClassPSPACE/TQBFHardMachine.lean =====

```
/-
Copyright (c) 2026 TCSlib contributors. All rights reserved.
Released under Apache 2.0 license as described in the file LICENSE.
Authors: Hydroxyi
-/
import TCSlib.Complexity.ClassPSPACE.TQBFHardSemantics
import TCSlib.Complexity.SpaceComplexity.Codec.Bridge

set_option maxHeartbeats 0
set_option relaxedAutoImplicit false
set_option autoImplicit false

/-!
# Acceptance as a short path of blocks

[AB09, Claim 4.4 and the proof of Theorem 4.13]: a space-bounded machine accepts `x` iff its
configuration graph has a path from the initial to an accepting configuration of length at
most the number of configurations. This file restates the bridge lemma of the configuration
codec (`Complexity.Codec.mem_iff_codeChain`, `Complexity.Codec.mem_of_codePath`) in the
form the `TQBF` reduction quantifies over: **blocks** of `w ≥ codeLen` bits whose first
`codeLen` bits are a code word, a one-step relation `blockStep` that is reflexive (so that
paths of length at most `2^w` are paths of length exactly `2^w`), and the midpoint recursion
`Complexity.TQBFHard.Mid` of `TQBFHardSemantics`.

Infrastructure for `Complexity.TQBF_PSPACEHard`; not itself a book result.

## Main definitions

* `Complexity.TQBFHard.codeLen` — the length of a code word.
* `Complexity.TQBFHard.blockInit`, `blockAcc`, `blockStep` — the three code-language tests on
  the code-word prefixes of blocks.

## Main results

* `Complexity.TQBFHard.mem_iff_mid` — membership is "some initial block reaches some
  accepting block in the midpoint recursion of depth `w`". [AB09, Claim 4.4(1), proof of
  Theorem 4.13]

## References

* [AB09] S. Arora, B. Barak, *Computational Complexity: A Modern Approach*,
  Cambridge University Press, 2009. (§4.1.1, Claim 4.4; §4.2, Theorem 4.13.)
-/

namespace Complexity

namespace TQBFHard

open Turing Codec LogProg

variable (N : FinNDTM Bool)

/-- The length `W(2s + 1) + wP n + 1` of a code word at input length `n` and radius `s`
(`Complexity.Codec.length_cfgWord`). -/
def codeLen (n s : ℕ) : ℕ := W N * (2 * s + 1) + wP n + 1

/-- The initial-code test on the first `L` bits of a block. -/
def blockInit (x : List Bool) (s L : ℕ) (β : List Bool) : Prop :=
  pairEncode x (pairEncode (β.take L) (Nat.bits s)) ∈ initLang N

/-- The accepting-code test on the first `L` bits of a block. -/
def blockAcc (x : List Bool) (s L : ℕ) (β : List Bool) : Prop :=
  pairEncode x (pairEncode (β.take L) (Nat.bits s)) ∈ acceptLang N

/-- **The one-step relation on blocks**: equal blocks, or blocks whose first `L` bits are a
step pair of the code (`Complexity.Codec.stepLang`). Reflexive by its first disjunct. -/
def blockStep (x : List Bool) (s L : ℕ) (β β' : List Bool) : Prop :=
  β = β' ∨ pairEncode x (pairEncode (β.take L) (pairEncode (β'.take L) (Nat.bits s))) ∈
    stepLang N

/-- With a reflexive one-step relation, a path can be lengthened. (Proved, by induction on
the excess, padding at the end.) -/
theorem steps_mono {w : ℕ} {E : List Bool → List Bool → Prop} (hE : ∀ B, E B B)
    {k k' : ℕ} (hk : k ≤ k') {A B : List Bool} (hB : B.length = w) (h : Steps w E k A B) :
    Steps w E k' A B := by
  obtain ⟨d, rfl⟩ : ∃ d, k' = k + d := ⟨k' - k, by omega⟩
  clear hk
  induction d with
  | zero => simpa using h
  | succ d ih => exact ⟨B, hB, ih, hE B⟩

/-- A block path is a path of code-word prefixes along step pairs. (Proved, by induction on
the path length.) -/
theorem steps_reflTransGen (x : List Bool) (s L w : ℕ) :
    ∀ (k : ℕ) (A B : List Bool), Steps w (blockStep N x s L) k A B →
      Relation.ReflTransGen (fun γ γ' : List Bool =>
        pairEncode x (pairEncode γ (pairEncode γ' (Nat.bits s))) ∈ stepLang N)
        (A.take L) (B.take L) := by
  intro k
  induction k with
  | zero => rintro A B rfl; exact Relation.ReflTransGen.refl
  | succ k ih =>
    rintro A B ⟨z, -, h1, h2 | h2⟩
    · subst h2; exact ih A z h1
    · exact (ih A z h1).tail h2

/-- A path of words along step pairs from the word of a code `u` reaches only words of codes,
along the code-level step relation `Complexity.Codec.StepRel`. (Proved, by induction along
the path.) -/
theorem reflTransGen_stepRel (x : List Bool) (s u : ℕ) {γ : List Bool}
    (h : Relation.ReflTransGen (fun γ γ' : List Bool =>
      pairEncode x (pairEncode γ (pairEncode γ' (Nat.bits s))) ∈ stepLang N) (Nat.bits u) γ) :
    ∀ c, γ = Nat.bits c → Relation.ReflTransGen (StepRel N x s) u c := by
  induction h with
  | refl =>
    intro c hc
    rw [bits_injective hc]
  | tail _ hst ih =>
    intro c hc
    subst hc
    obtain ⟨x', c₁, c₂, s', heq, -⟩ := id hst
    obtain ⟨rfl, h2⟩ := pairEncode_inj heq
    obtain ⟨h3, h4⟩ := pairEncode_inj h2
    obtain ⟨h5, h6⟩ := pairEncode_inj h4
    have hc₂ := bits_injective h5
    have hs := bits_injective h6
    subst hc₂ hs
    refine (ih c₁ h3).tail ?_
    show pairEncode x (pairEncode (Nat.bits c₁) (pairEncode (Nat.bits c) (Nat.bits s))) ∈
      stepLang N
    rw [← h3]
    exact hst

/-- **Acceptance as a block path** ([AB09, Claim 4.4(1)] in the form of the proof of
Theorem 4.13): let `N` decide `L` in space `sp`, `s ≥ sp |x|`, blocks of width
`w ≥ codeLen |x| s`, and `configBound |x| s ≤ 2^w`. Then `x ∈ L` iff there are blocks `A`,
`B` of width `w`, `A` initial and `B` accepting (on their code-word prefixes), with
`Mid w (blockStep …) w A B`.

**Proof sketch.** `Complexity.TQBFHard.mid_iff_steps` turns `Mid` into a path of exactly `2^w`
steps. (⇒) The chain of codes of `Complexity.Codec.mem_iff_codeChain`, each padded to width
`w` (code words have length `codeLen`, `Complexity.Codec.length_cfgWord`), is a block path of
length `t ≤ configBound ≤ 2^w`, lengthened by reflexive steps (`steps_mono`). (⇐) The block
path is a path of code-word prefixes (`steps_reflTransGen`) from the initial code's word, and
every word along it is a code's word (`reflTransGen_stepRel`), ending at an accepting code;
conclude with `Complexity.Codec.mem_of_codePath`. -/
theorem mem_iff_mid {L : Language Bool} {sp : ℕ → ℕ} (h : N.DecidesInSpace L sp)
    (x : List Bool) (s w : ℕ) (hs : sp x.length ≤ s) (hw : codeLen N x.length s ≤ w)
    (hR : N.configBound x.length s ≤ 2 ^ w) :
    x ∈ L ↔ ∃ A B : List Bool, A.length = w ∧ B.length = w ∧
      blockInit N x s (codeLen N x.length s) A ∧ blockAcc N x s (codeLen N x.length s) B ∧
      Mid w (blockStep N x s (codeLen N x.length s)) w A B := by
  set Lc := codeLen N x.length s with hLc
  have hrefl : ∀ B : List Bool, blockStep N x s Lc B B := fun B => Or.inl rfl
  constructor
  · intro hx
    obtain ⟨t, c, ht, hinit, hstep, hacc, -⟩ := (mem_iff_codeChain h x s hs).mp hx
    -- every code of the chain has a code word of length `Lc`
    have hlen : ∀ i ≤ t, (Nat.bits (c i)).length = Lc := by
      intro i hi
      rcases i with _ | i
      · rw [mem_initLang] at hinit
        rw [← hinit, bits_cfgCode, length_cfgWord, hLc, codeLen]
      · obtain ⟨-, -, -, C', -, -, hC'⟩ := (mem_stepLang N x _ _ s).mp (hstep i (by omega))
        rw [← hC', bits_cfgCode, length_cfgWord, hLc, codeLen]
    let β : ℕ → List Bool := fun i => Nat.bits (c i) ++ List.replicate (w - Lc) false
    have hβlen : ∀ i ≤ t, (β i).length = w := by
      intro i hi
      simp only [β, List.length_append, List.length_replicate, hlen i hi]
      omega
    have hβtake : ∀ i ≤ t, (β i).take Lc = Nat.bits (c i) := by
      intro i hi
      simp only [β]
      rw [List.take_append_of_le_length (by rw [hlen i hi]), List.take_of_length_le
        (by rw [hlen i hi])]
    have hpath : ∀ k ≤ t, Steps w (blockStep N x s Lc) k (β 0) (β k) := by
      intro k
      induction k with
      | zero => intro _; rfl
      | succ k ih =>
        intro hk
        refine ⟨β k, hβlen k (by omega), ih (by omega), Or.inr ?_⟩
        rw [hβtake k (by omega), hβtake (k + 1) hk]
        exact hstep k (by omega)
    refine ⟨β 0, β t, hβlen 0 (by omega), hβlen t le_rfl, ?_, ?_, ?_⟩
    · simp only [blockInit]
      rw [hβtake 0 (by omega)]
      exact hinit
    · simp only [blockAcc]
      rw [hβtake t le_rfl]
      exact hacc
    · rw [mid_iff_steps _ _ _ _ _ (hβlen 0 (by omega)) (hβlen t le_rfl)]
      exact steps_mono hrefl (ht.trans hR) (hβlen t le_rfl) (hpath t le_rfl)
  · rintro ⟨A, B, hA, hB, hinit, hacc, hmid⟩
    rw [mid_iff_steps _ _ _ _ _ hA hB] at hmid
    have hwords := steps_reflTransGen N x s Lc w _ A B hmid
    obtain ⟨x₁, u, s₁, h₁, hu⟩ := hinit
    obtain ⟨rfl, h₁'⟩ := pairEncode_inj h₁
    obtain ⟨hAu, hs₁⟩ := pairEncode_inj h₁'
    obtain rfl := bits_injective hs₁
    obtain ⟨x₂, v, s₂, h₂, hv⟩ := hacc
    obtain ⟨hx₂, h₂'⟩ := pairEncode_inj h₂
    obtain ⟨hBv, hs₂⟩ := pairEncode_inj h₂'
    obtain rfl := bits_injective hs₂
    subst hx₂
    rw [hAu] at hwords
    have hpath := reflTransGen_stepRel N x s u hwords v hBv
    refine mem_of_codePath h x s u v ((mem_initLang N x u s).mpr hu) hpath ?_
    exact (mem_acceptLang N x v s).mpr hv

end TQBFHard

end Complexity
```

/-

import TCSlib.Complexity.ClassPSPACE.TQBFHardBridge
import TCSlib.Complexity.Formulas.QBFEncoding

set_option maxHeartbeats 0
set_option relaxedAutoImplicit false
set_option autoImplicit false

/-!
# Parameters of the `TQBF` reduction, and its quantifier prefix

For a machine `N` deciding a language in space `d (n^c + 1)`, the reduction uses the radius
`2d (n + 1)^c` and blocks (and levels) of width `w = A (n + 1)^(c + 1)` with the machine
constant `A = wCoef N d`. This file proves that this width holds a code word
(`vlen_le_vwid`) and that `2^w` steps suffice to reach every configuration
(`configBound_le_two_pow`), and that the bits of the level part of the quantifier prefix
(`w` levels of `∃^w ∀^w ∀^w`) are polynomial-time computable (`polyTimeComputable_levelBits`,
a round loop over `Complexity.polyTimeComputable_of_loop`).

Infrastructure for `Complexity.TQBF_PSPACEHard`; not itself a book result.

## Main definitions

* `Complexity.TQBFHard.wCoef` — the width coefficient.
* `Complexity.TQBFHard.levelBits` — the prefix bits of `r` levels.

## Main results

* `Complexity.TQBFHard.vlen_le_vwid`, `Complexity.TQBFHard.configBound_le_two_pow` — the
  width suffices. [AB09, Claim 4.4(1): `2^{O(s(n))}` configurations]
* `Complexity.TQBFHard.map_quantBit_levelQuants` — the prefix bits of the levels.
* `Complexity.TQBFHard.polyTimeComputable_levelBits` — they are polynomial-time.

## References

* [AB09] S. Arora, B. Barak, *Computational Complexity: A Modern Approach*,
  Cambridge University Press, 2009. (§4.1.1, Claim 4.4; §4.2, Theorem 4.13.)
-/

namespace Complexity

namespace TQBFHard

open Turing Codec QBF

/-! ### The width -/

variable (N : FinNDTM Bool) (d c : ℕ)

/-- **The width coefficient** of a machine `N` with space constant `d`. -/
def wCoef : ℕ := 4 * d * W N + W N + 12 * N.k * d + 3 * N.k + 2 * Fintype.card N.State + 8

/-- The binary length of `n + 1` is at most `n + 1`. -/
theorem wP_le (n : ℕ) : wP n ≤ n + 1 :=
  LogProg.length_bits_le (Nat.lt_two_pow_self)

/-- **The width holds a code word**: `codeLen ≤ wCoef · (n + 1)^(c + 1)`. -/
theorem vlen_le_vwid (n : ℕ) : vlen N d c n ≤ vwid (wCoef N d) (c + 1) n := by
  have hQP : (n + 1) ^ c ≤ (n + 1) ^ (c + 1) := Nat.pow_le_pow_right (by omega) (by omega)
  have hP1 : 1 ≤ (n + 1) ^ c := Nat.one_le_pow _ _ (by omega)
  have hnP : n + 1 ≤ (n + 1) ^ (c + 1) := by
    calc n + 1 = (n + 1) ^ 1 := (pow_one _).symm
      _ ≤ _ := Nat.pow_le_pow_right (by omega) (by omega)
  have hw := wP_le n
  set P := (n + 1) ^ (c + 1)
  set Q := (n + 1) ^ c
  have h1 : 4 * d * W N * Q ≤ 4 * d * W N * P := Nat.mul_le_mul_left _ hQP
  have h2 : W N ≤ W N * P := Nat.le_mul_of_pos_right _ (by omega)
  have h4 : 2 * P ≤ (12 * N.k * d + 3 * N.k + 2 * Fintype.card N.State + 8) * P :=
    Nat.mul_le_mul_right _ (by omega)
  have e1 : vlen N d c n = 4 * d * W N * Q + W N + wP n + 1 := by
    simp only [vlen, codeLen, vrad, Q]; ring
  have e2 : vwid (wCoef N d) (c + 1) n = 4 * d * W N * P + W N * P +
      (12 * N.k * d + 3 * N.k + 2 * Fintype.card N.State + 8) * P := by
    simp only [vwid, wCoef, P]; ring
  rw [e1, e2]
  omega

/-- `3m ≤ 2^(2m)`. -/
private theorem three_mul_le (m : ℕ) : 3 * m ≤ 2 ^ (2 * m) := by
  have h1 : m + 1 ≤ 2 ^ m := Nat.lt_two_pow_self
  have h2 : 2 ^ (2 * m) = 2 ^ m * 2 ^ m := by rw [two_mul, pow_add]
  have h3 : 3 * m ≤ (m + 1) * (m + 1) := by nlinarith [Nat.le_mul_self m]
  rw [h2]
  exact h3.trans (Nat.mul_le_mul h1 h1)

/-- **`2^w` steps suffice** ([AB09, Claim 4.4(1)]): the vertex count at radius
`2d (n + 1)^c` is at most `2^w`.

**Proof sketch.** `3(Q + 1) ≤ 2^{2(Q+1)}`, `n + 2 ≤ 2^{n+1}`, `3^e ≤ 2^{2e}` and
`(2s + 1)^k ≤ 2^{k(2s+1)}`, so the count is at most `2^X` with
`X = 2(Q + 1) + (n + 1) + 3k(2s + 1) ≤ w`. -/
theorem configBound_le_two_pow (n : ℕ) :
    N.configBound n (vrad d c n) ≤ 2 ^ vwid (wCoef N d) (c + 1) n := by
  set s := vrad d c n
  set e := N.k * (2 * s + 1)
  have b1 : 3 * (Fintype.card N.State + 1) ≤ 2 ^ (2 * (Fintype.card N.State + 1)) :=
    three_mul_le _
  have b2 : n + 2 ≤ 2 ^ (n + 1) := Nat.lt_two_pow_self
  have key3 : ∀ m : ℕ, 3 ^ m ≤ 2 ^ (2 * m) := fun m => by
    rw [pow_mul]; exact Nat.pow_le_pow_left (by norm_num) m
  have b3 : 3 ^ e ≤ 2 ^ (2 * e) := key3 e
  have b4 : (2 * s + 1) ^ N.k ≤ 2 ^ e := by
    have : 2 * s + 1 < 2 ^ (2 * s + 1) := Nat.lt_two_pow_self
    calc (2 * s + 1) ^ N.k ≤ (2 ^ (2 * s + 1)) ^ N.k := Nat.pow_le_pow_left this.le _
      _ = 2 ^ e := by rw [← pow_mul]; congr 1; simp only [e]; ring
  have hX : 2 * (Fintype.card N.State + 1) + (n + 1) + 2 * e + e ≤
      vwid (wCoef N d) (c + 1) n := by
    have hQP : (n + 1) ^ c ≤ (n + 1) ^ (c + 1) := Nat.pow_le_pow_right (by omega) (by omega)
    have hnP : n + 1 ≤ (n + 1) ^ (c + 1) := by
      calc n + 1 = (n + 1) ^ 1 := (pow_one _).symm
        _ ≤ _ := Nat.pow_le_pow_right (by omega) (by omega)
    have hP1 : 1 ≤ (n + 1) ^ (c + 1) := by omega
    set P := (n + 1) ^ (c + 1)
    set Q := (n + 1) ^ c
    have h1 : 12 * N.k * d * Q ≤ 12 * N.k * d * P := Nat.mul_le_mul_left _ hQP
    have e1 : 2 * (Fintype.card N.State + 1) + (n + 1) + 2 * e + e =
        2 * Fintype.card N.State + 3 + n + 12 * N.k * d * Q + 3 * N.k := by
      simp only [e, s, vrad, Q]; ring
    have e2 : vwid (wCoef N d) (c + 1) n = 4 * d * W N * P + W N * P + 12 * N.k * d * P +
        3 * N.k * P + 2 * Fintype.card N.State * P + 8 * P := by
      simp only [vwid, wCoef, P]; ring
    have h3 : 3 * N.k ≤ 3 * N.k * P := Nat.le_mul_of_pos_right _ (by omega)
    have h5 : 2 * Fintype.card N.State ≤ 2 * Fintype.card N.State * P :=
      Nat.le_mul_of_pos_right _ (by omega)
    rw [e1, e2]
    omega
  calc N.configBound n s
      = (3 * (Fintype.card N.State + 1)) * (n + 2) * 3 ^ e * (2 * s + 1) ^ N.k := by
        simp only [FinNDTM.configBound, e]; ring
    _ ≤ 2 ^ (2 * (Fintype.card N.State + 1)) * 2 ^ (n + 1) * 2 ^ (2 * e) * 2 ^ e := by
        gcongr
    _ = 2 ^ (2 * (Fintype.card N.State + 1) + (n + 1) + 2 * e + e) := by
        simp only [pow_add]
    _ ≤ _ := Nat.pow_le_pow_right (by norm_num) hX

/-! ### The prefix bits of the levels -/

/-- The prefix bits of `r` levels of width `w`: per level `1^w 0^{2w}` (`∃` is `1`). -/
def levelBits (w r : ℕ) : List Bool :=
  (List.range r).flatMap fun _ => List.replicate w true ++ List.replicate (2 * w) false

/-- The levels' quantifiers are written as `levelBits`. (Proved, by induction on `r`.) -/
theorem map_quantBit_levelQuants (w r : ℕ) :
    (levelQuants w r).map quantBit = levelBits w r := by
  induction r with
  | zero => rfl
  | succ r ih =>
    simp only [levelQuants, List.map_append, List.map_replicate, ih, levelBits,
      List.range_succ_eq_map, List.flatMap_cons, List.flatMap_map]
    simp only [quantBit, two_mul, List.replicate_add, List.append_assoc]

/-- The one-pass map writing a `0` for every letter. -/
def zeroes (l : List Bool) : List Bool :=
  transduce (σ := Unit) (fun _ _ => ()) (fun _ _ => some false) () l

/-- `zeroes` writes `|l|` zeroes. -/
theorem zeroes_eq (l : List Bool) : zeroes l = List.replicate l.length false := by
  induction l with
  | nil => rfl
  | cons b l ih => simp only [zeroes, transduce] at ih ⊢; simp [ih, List.replicate_succ]

/-- The round of the level-bit loop: drop one letter of the countdown. -/
def lbStep (s : List Bool) : List Bool := pairEncode (pairFstD s) ((pairSndD s).drop 1)

/-- The chunk of the level-bit loop: `1^w 0^{2w}` while the countdown is nonempty. -/
def lbChunk (s : List Bool) : List Bool :=
  if pairSndD s = [] then [] else pairFstD s ++ (zeroes (pairFstD s) ++ zeroes (pairFstD s))

/-- The round does not lengthen a state beyond `max |s| 2`. -/
private theorem length_lbStep (s : List Bool) : (lbStep s).length ≤ max s.length 2 := by
  cases hd : pairDecode s with
  | none =>
    have hf : pairFstD s = [] := by simp [pairFstD, hd]
    have hs : pairSndD s = [] := by simp [pairSndD, hd]
    simp [lbStep, hf, hs, length_pairEncode]
  | some uv =>
    obtain ⟨u, v⟩ := uv
    have he := eq_pairEncode_of_pairDecode s u v hd
    subst he
    simp only [lbStep, pairFstD_pairEncode, pairSndD_pairEncode, length_pairEncode,
      List.length_drop]
    omega

/-- Iterates of the round on a pair drop from the countdown. -/
private theorem lbStep_iterate (u v : List Bool) (i : ℕ) :
    lbStep^[i] (pairEncode u v) = pairEncode u (v.drop i) := by
  induction i with
  | zero => rfl
  | succ i ih =>
    rw [Function.iterate_succ_apply', ih]
    simp [lbStep, List.drop_drop]

/-- **The prefix bits of the levels are polynomial-time**: for a polynomial-time unary width
`w x`, the word `levelBits (w x) (w x)` is polynomial-time computable.

**Proof sketch.** `Complexity.polyTimeComputable_of_loop` on the state `⟨1^w, 1^w⟩`: each
round emits `1^w 0^{2w}` while the countdown is nonempty and drops one countdown letter
(`lbStep`, `lbChunk`); states never grow beyond `max |s| 2`, and the round budget
`|init| + 2` exceeds `w`. -/
theorem polyTimeComputable_levelBits {w : List Bool → ℕ}
    (hw : PolyTimeComputable fun x => List.replicate (w x) true) :
    PolyTimeComputable fun x => levelBits (w x) (w x) := by
  have hstep : PolyTimeComputable lbStep :=
    polyTimeComputable_pairFstD.pairEncode
      (polyTimeComputable_tail.comp polyTimeComputable_pairSndD)
  have hz : PolyTimeComputable zeroes := polyTimeComputable_transduce _ _ _
  have hchunk : PolyTimeComputable lbChunk := by
    have hne := polyTimeComputable_isNil.comp polyTimeComputable_pairSndD
    have := polyTimeComputable_ite hne (polyTimeComputable_const [])
      (polyTimeComputable_pairFstD.append ((hz.comp polyTimeComputable_pairFstD).append
        (hz.comp polyTimeComputable_pairFstD)))
    convert this using 1
    funext s
    simp only [lbChunk, Function.comp]
    by_cases h : pairSndD s = [] <;> simp [h]
  have hinit : PolyTimeComputable fun x =>
      pairEncode (List.replicate (w x) true) (List.replicate (w x) true) := hw.pairEncode hw
  refine BlockLoop.polyTimeComputable_of_loop hstep hchunk hinit 1 1 2 (fun s i => ?_) (fun x => ?_)
  · have key : ∀ j, (lbStep^[j] s).length ≤ max s.length 2 := by
      intro j
      induction j with
      | zero => exact le_max_left _ _
      | succ j ih =>
        rw [Function.iterate_succ_apply']
        exact (length_lbStep _).trans (max_le ih (le_max_right _ _))
    have := key i
    simp only [pow_one]
    omega
  · simp only [lbStep_iterate, length_pairEncode, List.length_replicate, pow_one, one_mul]
    set m := w x
    have hcnt : 2 * m + 2 + m + 1 + 1 = m + (2 * m + 4) := by ring
    rw [hcnt, List.range_add, List.flatMap_append]
    have h2 : ((List.range (2 * m + 4)).map (m + ·)).flatMap
        (fun i => lbChunk (pairEncode (List.replicate m true)
          ((List.replicate m true).drop i))) = [] := by
      simp only [List.flatMap_eq_nil_iff, List.mem_map, List.mem_range]
      rintro _ ⟨j, _, rfl⟩
      simp [lbChunk, List.drop_eq_nil_of_le]
    rw [h2, List.append_nil, levelBits]
    apply List.flatMap_congr
    intro i hi
    rw [List.mem_range] at hi
    have hne : (List.replicate m true).drop i ≠ [] := by
      simp; omega
    simp only [lbChunk, pairSndD_pairEncode, pairFstD_pairEncode, hne, if_false, zeroes_eq,
      List.length_replicate, two_mul, List.replicate_add]

end TQBFHard

end Complexity
```
