```
set_option maxHeartbeats 0
set_option relaxedAutoImplicit false
set_option autoImplicit false

/-!
# Configuration graphs of nondeterministic machines

[AB09, §4.1.1]: the configuration graph `G_{M,x}` of a machine on an input —
vertices the configurations, edges the one-step transitions (out-degree at most
two for a binary-choice NDTM) — together with the counting half of Claim 4.4(1)
for nondeterministic branches. This is phase P4.2 of `AroraBarakChapters3-4Plan.md`. The
exponential-time simulation ([AB09, Theorem 4.2, third inclusion]), `NL ⊆ P`, and the
coarseness of polynomial-time reductions below `P` ([AB09, Exercise 4.3]) were stated here;
their proof runs a breadth-first search over the configuration codec
(`TCSlib.Complexity.SpaceComplexity.Codec`), which imports this module, so they now live in
`TCSlib.Complexity.SpaceComplexity.ExpTime` with their statements unchanged. Savitch's
theorem, the other consumer of this layer, is `TCSlib.Complexity.SpaceComplexity.Savitch`.

**Status: graph lemmas proved (phase P4.2, batch S1a).** The four graph contracts are proved;
`Complexity.NSPACE_subset_exp_dtime`, `Complexity.NL_subset_P` and
`Complexity.polyTimeReducible_of_mem_NL` are proved in
`TCSlib.Complexity.SpaceComplexity.ExpTime` (2026-10-14). The private `s1b_*` helpers below
belong to the superseded record-table route of the S1b partial fill and have no consumer.
`spaceConstructible_logSpace` is proved (B3a).

## Design

* **The vertex is a core plus a bounded output summary.** The received
  deterministic counting layer (`Turing.MultiTapeTM.ConfigCount`) counts
  *cores* — configurations without their output tapes — which is sound for
  halting-time bounds because output is write-only. For *acceptance* along a
  branch it is **not** sufficient by itself: acceptance means output exactly
  `[true]` at a halted configuration, and splicing out a cycle between equal
  cores could delete the branch's one emission (the P0 reception audit's
  fitness note, `audits/ch34-p0-findings.md` §7, anticipated exactly this). The
  vertex therefore carries `Turing.OutSummary` — the three-valued quotient of
  the output by its relation to `[true]`: still empty, exactly `[true]`, or
  irrecoverably dead — which is compatible with the append-only output
  discipline and multiplies the core count by three
  (`Turing.FinNDTM.configBound`).
* **The graph is the step relation, not a finite object**: `Turing.NDTM.CfgStep`
  is a relation on configurations, with `Relation.ReflTransGen` as
  reachability; the finite counting enters only through the configuration-count
  bounds (`acceptsWithin_of_spaceUsedWith_le`, proved).
  Efficient vertex *encoding* reuses `Turing.MultiTapeTM.ConfigCount.coreCode`;
  the adjacency CNF of Claim 4.4(2) is deliberately phase P4.3.
* **Facade wiring**: root-wired while the P4.1 gate was live; since that
  gate closed (round 1, PASS), the `SpaceComplexity.lean` facade carries this
  module and `Savitch`.

## Main definitions

* `Turing.OutSummary`, `Turing.outSummary` — the three-valued output summary.
* `Turing.NDTM.coreSum` — the configuration-graph vertex: core plus summary.
* `Turing.NDTM.CfgStep` — the edge relation (one `stepWith`, either choice).
  [AB09, §4.1.1: out-degree at most two]
* `Turing.FinNDTM.configBound` — the vertex count at window radius `s`:
  three times the deterministic `configBound` formula. [AB09, Claim 4.4(1)]

## Main results

* `Turing.NDTM.reflTransGen_cfgStep_iff` — reachability is the choice-word run.
* `Turing.NDTM.coreSum_stepWith` — a step's vertex depends only on the vertex.
* `Turing.FinNDTM.acceptsWithin_of_spaceUsedWith_le` — Claim 4.4(1),
  acceptance form: a space-`s` accepting branch shortens to the vertex count.
* `Turing.FinNDTM.DecidesInSpace.mem_iff_acceptsWithin_configBound` — the
  packaged interface the simulations consume.
* `Turing.outSummary_eq_accept_iff` — the summary recognizes exactly `[true]`.
* `Turing.outSummary_append_congr` — a common output suffix preserves summary equality.
* `Turing.NDTM.coreSum_runWith` — a common choice word preserves vertex equality.
* `Turing.FinNDTM.not_acceptsWithin_zero` — acceptance requires a transition.

## References

* [AB09] S. Arora, B. Barak, *Computational Complexity: A Modern Approach*,
  Cambridge University Press, 2009. (§4.1.1, Claim 4.4, Theorem 4.2;
  §4.1.2; Exercise 4.3.)
-/

namespace Turing

variable {k : ℕ} {S : Type} {x : List Bool}

/-- The three-valued summary of an append-only output word relative to the
acceptance target `[true]`: still empty, exactly `[true]`, or dead — no
further appending can reach `[true]` from a dead output. The quotient the
configuration-graph vertex carries alongside the core (see the module
docstring for why the core alone cannot certify acceptance). -/
inductive OutSummary where
  /-- nothing emitted yet -/
  | empty
  /-- the output is exactly `[true]` -/
  | accept
  /-- the output can no longer become `[true]` -/
  | dead
deriving DecidableEq

/-- The summary of an output word: `[]` is `empty`, `[true]` is `accept`,
everything else is `dead`. Compatible with appending — the summary of
`out ++ e` is a function of the summary of `out` and `e` alone, which is what
makes the vertex sound for splicing arguments. -/
def outSummary : List Bool → OutSummary
  | [] => .empty
  | [true] => .accept
  | _ => .dead

/-- An output summary accepts exactly the singleton true output. [AB09, §4.1.1]

**Proof sketch.** Inspect the empty, singleton, and longer output words. -/
theorem outSummary_eq_accept_iff (u : List Bool) : outSummary u = .accept ↔ u = [true] := by
  cases u with
  | nil => simp [outSummary]
  | cons a u => cases u <;> cases a <;> simp [outSummary]

/-- Equal summaries remain equal after appending a common output suffix.
[AB09, §4.1.1]

**Proof sketch.** An empty prefix contributes nothing, an accepting prefix
survives only an empty suffix, and a dead prefix stays dead. -/
theorem outSummary_append_congr {u v : List Bool} (h : outSummary u = outSummary v)
    (e : List Bool) : outSummary (u ++ e) = outSummary (v ++ e) := by
  have table (a : List Bool) : outSummary (a ++ e) =
      match outSummary a with
      | .empty => outSummary e
      | .accept => if e = [] then .accept else .dead
      | .dead => .dead := by
    cases a with
    | nil => rfl
    | cons b a => cases a <;> cases b <;> cases e <;> simp [outSummary]
  rw [table, table, h]

/-- Heads and all nonblank work cells lie in the finite coding window. -/
private def InWindow (s : ℕ) (c : Cfg k Bool S x) : Prop :=
  ∀ i, |c.workTapePos i| ≤ s ∧ ∀ z, c.workTapes i z ≠ none → |z| ≤ s

/-- The graph window and the public record window agree. This is the single
bridge allowed by S1b ground rule 10; S1a's declarations remain unchanged.

**Proof sketch.** Separate the head bounds and contrapose the cell bounds. -/
private theorem inWindow_iff_cfgInWindow (s : ℕ) (c : Cfg k Bool S x) :
    InWindow s c ↔ c.InWindow s := by
  constructor
  · intro h
    refine ⟨fun i => (h i).1, ?_⟩
    intro i z hz
    by_contra nonblank
    exact (not_le_of_gt hz) ((h i).2 z nonblank)
  · rintro ⟨heads, cells⟩ i
    refine ⟨heads i, ?_⟩
    intro z nonblank
    by_contra outside
    exact nonblank (cells i z (lt_of_not_ge outside))

namespace NDTM

/-- The configuration-graph **vertex** of a configuration: its core (state,
input position, work tapes, work heads — `Turing.MultiTapeTM.ConfigCount.core`)
together with the output summary. Two configurations with equal vertices have
equal futures up to output-suffix equality, which is exactly what acceptance
needs. [AB09, §4.1.1] -/
def coreSum (c : Cfg k Bool S x) :
    (Option S × Fin (x.length + 2) × (Fin k → ℤ → Option Bool) × (Fin k → ℤ)) ×
      OutSummary :=
  (MultiTapeTM.ConfigCount.core c, outSummary c.output)

/-- The configuration-graph **edge relation** of [AB09, §4.1.1]: `c` steps to
`c'` under some choice bit. A binary-choice NDTM gives out-degree at most two;
a halted configuration self-loops (`Turing.NDTM.stepWith_of_halt`). -/
def CfgStep (tm : NDTM k Bool S) (c c' : Cfg k Bool S x) : Prop :=
  ∃ b : Bool, tm.stepWith b c = c'

/-- **Reachability in the configuration graph is the choice-word run**
(proved — phase P4.2): `c'` is `Relation.ReflTransGen`-reachable
from `c` along `Turing.NDTM.CfgStep` iff some choice word runs `c` to `c'`.
This is the dictionary between [AB09]'s graph language and the campaign's
`runWith` semantics.

**Proof sketch.** Forward: induction on the reflexive-transitive chain,
appending the step's choice bit (`Turing.NDTM.runWith_append` at a singleton).
Backward: induction on the word, `Relation.ReflTransGen.head` at each consumed
bit (`Turing.NDTM.runWith_cons`). -/
theorem reflTransGen_cfgStep_iff (tm : NDTM k Bool S) (c c' : Cfg k Bool S x) :
    Relation.ReflTransGen (tm.CfgStep) c c' ↔ ∃ w : List Bool, tm.runWith w c = c' := by
  constructor
  · intro h
    induction h with
    | refl => exact ⟨[], rfl⟩
    | @tail d e _ edge ih =>
      obtain ⟨w, rfl⟩ := ih
      obtain ⟨b, rfl⟩ := edge
      exact ⟨w ++ [b], by rw [runWith_append, runWith_cons, runWith_nil]⟩
  · rintro ⟨w, rfl⟩
    induction w generalizing c with
    | nil => exact Relation.ReflTransGen.refl
    | cons b w ih => exact Relation.ReflTransGen.head ⟨b, rfl⟩ (ih _)

/-- The emitted symbol is determined by the core, independently of the output history.

**Proof sketch.** Destructure the configurations and identify their four core fields;
the transition reads precisely those fields. -/
private theorem outputSymbol_congr (M : MultiTapeTM k Bool S) {c d : Cfg k Bool S x}
    (h : MultiTapeTM.ConfigCount.core c = MultiTapeTM.ConfigCount.core d) :
    M.outputSymbol c = M.outputSymbol d := by
  cases c
  cases d
  simp only [MultiTapeTM.ConfigCount.core, Prod.mk.injEq] at h
  rcases h with ⟨rfl, rfl, rfl, rfl⟩
  rfl

/-- **A step's vertex depends only on the vertex** (proved — phase
P4.2; the nondeterministic, summary-carrying analogue of
`Turing.MultiTapeTM.ConfigCount.core_step`): configurations with equal
`coreSum` have equal `coreSum` after one `stepWith` under the same choice bit.

**Proof sketch.** The action is selected from the state and the scanned
symbols, all read off the core (as in `core_step`: `Cfg.inputSymbol` and
`Cfg.workTapeSymbols` are core-determined), so the two steps apply the same
action to cores that agree; the new output is the old output appended by the
action's emission, and `Turing.outSummary` of an append is a function of the
old summary and the emission (case analysis on the three summary values and
the optional emitted bit — the compatibility fact of the summary quotient). -/
theorem coreSum_stepWith (tm : NDTM k Bool S) (b : Bool) {c d : Cfg k Bool S x}
    (h : coreSum c = coreSum d) :
    coreSum (tm.stepWith b c) = coreSum (tm.stepWith b d) := by
  change (MultiTapeTM.ConfigCount.core _, outSummary _) =
    (MultiTapeTM.ConfigCount.core _, outSummary _)
  have hc := congrArg Prod.fst h
  have ho := congrArg Prod.snd h
  rw [stepWith_eq_fixChoice_step, stepWith_eq_fixChoice_step]
  apply Prod.ext (MultiTapeTM.ConfigCount.core_step _ hc)
  rw [MultiTapeTM.step_output, MultiTapeTM.step_output, outputSymbol_congr _ hc]
  exact outSummary_append_congr ho _

/-- A common choice word preserves equality of configuration-graph vertices.
[AB09, §4.1.1]

**Proof sketch.** Induct on the word and apply the one-step congruence. -/
theorem coreSum_runWith (tm : NDTM k Bool S) (w : List Bool)
    {c d : Cfg k Bool S x} (h : coreSum c = coreSum d) :
    coreSum (tm.runWith w c) = coreSum (tm.runWith w d) := by
  induction w generalizing c d with
  | nil => exact h
  | cons b w ih => exact ih (coreSum_stepWith tm b h)

/-- Successive choice prefixes either leave the configuration fixed or apply one action.

**Proof sketch.** Append the optional next choice bit. If it exists, use its
deterministic slice; a halted slice is the identity. -/
private theorem take_succ_action (tm : NDTM k Bool S) (w : List Bool)
    (c : Cfg k Bool S x) (j : ℕ) :
    tm.runWith (w.take (j + 1)) c = tm.runWith (w.take j) c ∨
      ∃ a : Action k Bool S,
        tm.runWith (w.take (j + 1)) c = a.apply (tm.runWith (w.take j) c) := by
  rw [List.take_succ, runWith_append]
  cases w[j]? with
  | none => exact Or.inl rfl
  | some b =>
    simp only [Option.toList_some, runWith_cons, runWith_nil, stepWith_eq_fixChoice_step]
    unfold MultiTapeTM.step
    cases (tm.runWith (w.take j) c).state with
    | none => exact Or.inl rfl
    | some q => exact Or.inr ⟨_, rfl⟩

/-- A position visited from initialization has absolute value below the visited-set size.

**Proof sketch.** Instantiate the shared unit-step image bound with the prefix runs;
`take_succ_action` and the action head-motion bound supply unit steps. -/
private theorem abs_lt_card_visitedWith (tm : NDTM k Bool S) (w : List Bool)
    (i : Fin k) {z : ℤ} (hz : z ∈ tm.visitedWith w (tm.initCfg x) i) :
    |z| < (tm.visitedWith w (tm.initCfg x) i).card := by
  apply MultiTapeTM.ConfigCount.abs_lt_card_image_of_unitSteps
    (fun j => (tm.runWith (w.take j) (tm.initCfg x)).workTapePos i) (by simp) _ w.length hz
  intro j
  dsimp only
  rcases take_succ_action tm w (tm.initCfg x) j with same | ⟨a, step⟩
  · rw [same]; simp
  · rw [step]; exact workTapePos_apply_le a _ i

/-- Every nonblank cell of a choice-word run from initialization has been visited.

**Proof sketch.** Instantiate the shared blank-tape action-sequence lemma with
prefix runs and their single `take_succ_action` decomposition. -/
private theorem mem_visitedWith_of_ne_none (tm : NDTM k Bool S) (w : List Bool)
    (i : Fin k) (z : ℤ) (hz : (tm.runWith w (tm.initCfg x)).workTapes i z ≠ none) :
    z ∈ tm.visitedWith w (tm.initCfg x) i := by
  exact MultiTapeTM.ConfigCount.mem_image_workTapePos_of_ne_none
    (fun j => tm.runWith (w.take j) (tm.initCfg x)) (by simp)
    (take_succ_action tm w (tm.initCfg x)) w.length i z
    (by simpa only [List.take_length] using hz)

/-- Taking a choice prefix only removes visited positions.

**Proof sketch.** Each prefix of the shortened word is the same prefix of the
original word, with an index no larger than either word's length. -/
private theorem visitedWith_take_subset (tm : NDTM k Bool S) (w : List Bool)
    (c : Cfg k Bool S x) (j : ℕ) (i : Fin k) :
    tm.visitedWith (w.take j) c i ⊆ tm.visitedWith w c i := by
  apply Finset.image_subset_iff.mpr
  intro n hn
  have hn' : n ≤ min j w.length := by simpa using Nat.le_of_lt_succ (Finset.mem_range.mp hn)
  apply Finset.mem_image.mpr
  refine ⟨n, Finset.mem_range.mpr (by omega), ?_⟩
  rw [List.take_take, Nat.min_eq_left (by omega : n ≤ j)]

/-- A space-bounded branch has every prefix in its coding window.

**Proof sketch.** A tape's visited-set cardinality is at most the total space.
Heads are in the visited set; nonblank cells are in a prefix's visited set,
which is contained in that of the whole word. Apply the shared position bound. -/
private theorem runWith_take_inWindow (tm : NDTM k Bool S) (w : List Bool) {s : ℕ}
    (hs : tm.spaceUsedWith w (tm.initCfg x) ≤ s) (j : ℕ) :
    InWindow s (tm.runWith (w.take j) (tm.initCfg x)) := by
  intro i
  have card_bound : (tm.visitedWith w (tm.initCfg x) i).card ≤ s :=
    (Finset.single_le_sum (f := fun i => (tm.visitedWith w (tm.initCfg x) i).card)
      (fun _ _ => Nat.zero_le _) (Finset.mem_univ i)).trans hs
  have bounded (z : ℤ) (hz : z ∈ tm.visitedWith (w.take j) (tm.initCfg x) i) : |z| ≤ s := by
    have hz' := visitedWith_take_subset tm w (tm.initCfg x) j i hz
    have small := abs_lt_card_visitedWith tm w i hz'
    omega
  constructor
  · apply bounded
    apply Finset.mem_image.mpr
    exact ⟨(w.take j).length, Finset.mem_range.mpr (Nat.lt_succ_self _), by
      rw [List.take_length]⟩
  · intro z hz
    exact bounded z (mem_visitedWith_of_ne_none tm (w.take j) i z hz)

/-- Window validity depends only on the configuration-graph vertex. -/
private theorem inWindow_of_coreSum_eq {s : ℕ} {c d : Cfg k Bool S x}
    (h : coreSum c = coreSum d) (hd : InWindow s d) : InWindow s c := by
  have tapes : c.workTapes = d.workTapes := congrArg (fun v => v.1.2.2.1) h
  have heads : c.workTapePos = d.workTapePos := congrArg (fun v => v.1.2.2.2) h
  simpa only [InWindow, tapes, heads] using hd

/-- Deleting a segment between equal vertices preserves the final vertex and
makes every new prefix vertex an old prefix vertex. [AB09, §4.1.1]

**Proof sketch.** Before the cut, prefixes agree. After the cut, run the same
remaining choices from the two equal vertices and use `coreSum_runWith`.
The old index is the later cut index plus the length traversed after the cut. -/
private theorem splice_vertices (tm : NDTM k Bool S) (c : Cfg k Bool S x)
    (w : List Bool) {a b : ℕ} (hab : a ≤ b) (hb : b ≤ w.length)
    (same : coreSum (tm.runWith (w.take a) c) = coreSum (tm.runWith (w.take b) c)) :
    coreSum (tm.runWith (w.take a ++ w.drop b) c) = coreSum (tm.runWith w c) ∧
    ∀ j ≤ (w.take a ++ w.drop b).length, ∃ l ≤ w.length,
      coreSum (tm.runWith ((w.take a ++ w.drop b).take j) c) =
        coreSum (tm.runWith (w.take l) c) := by
  have ha : a ≤ w.length := hab.trans hb
  constructor
  · simpa only [← runWith_append, List.take_append_drop] using coreSum_runWith tm (w.drop b) same
  · intro j hj
    by_cases before : j ≤ a
    · refine ⟨j, before.trans ha, ?_⟩
      rw [List.take_append_of_le_length (by simpa [List.length_take_of_le ha] using before),
        List.take_take, Nat.min_eq_left before]
    · refine ⟨b + (j - a), ?_, ?_⟩
      · simp only [List.length_append, List.length_take_of_le ha, List.length_drop] at hj
        omega
      · rw [List.take_append, List.take_take, Nat.min_eq_right (by omega : a ≤ j),
          List.length_take_of_le ha, List.take_add, runWith_append, runWith_append]
        exact coreSum_runWith tm ((w.drop b).take (j - a)) same

end NDTM

namespace FinNDTM

/-- The configuration-graph **vertex count** of `N` on inputs of length `n`
with window radius `s`: three (the output summaries) times the deterministic
core-code count of `Turing.FinTM.configBound` —
`3 · (|Q| + 1) · (n + 2) · 3^{k(2s+1)} · (2s+1)^k`. [AB09, Claim 4.4(1), with
the campaign's explicit constants] -/
def configBound (N : FinNDTM Bool) (n s : ℕ) : ℕ :=
  3 * ((Fintype.card N.State + 1) * (n + 2) * 3 ^ (N.k * (2 * s + 1)) *
    (2 * s + 1) ^ N.k)

/-- Encode the three output summaries without adding a finiteness instance. -/
private def sumCode : OutSummary → Fin 3
  | .empty => 0
  | .accept => 1
  | .dead => 2

/-- Distinct summaries have distinct three-element codes. -/
private theorem sumCode_injective : Function.Injective sumCode := by
  intro a b h
  cases a <;> cases b <;> simp_all [sumCode]

/-- Pairwise-distinct vertices of windowed configurations number at most the
configuration bound. [AB09, Claim 4.4(1)]

**Proof sketch.** Pair the received finite core code with the three-element
summary code. Windowedness supplies exactly the hypotheses of `coreCode_inj`.
The resulting injection has a finite codomain of the displayed cardinality. -/
private theorem count_windowed_vertices (N : FinNDTM Bool) (x : List Bool) (s t : ℕ)
    (cs : ℕ → Cfg N.k Bool N.State x)
    (window : ∀ j ≤ t, InWindow s (cs j))
    (distinct : Set.InjOn (fun j => NDTM.coreSum (cs j)) (Finset.range (t + 1))) :
    t + 1 ≤ N.configBound x.length s := by
  classical
  let code j := (MultiTapeTM.ConfigCount.coreCode s (cs j), sumCode (outSummary (cs j).output))
  have injective : Set.InjOn code (Finset.range (t + 1)) := by
    intro a ha b hb eqcode
    apply distinct ha hb
    apply Prod.ext
    · exact MultiTapeTM.ConfigCount.coreCode_inj s
        (window a (Nat.le_of_lt_succ (Finset.mem_range.mp ha)))
        (window b (Nat.le_of_lt_succ (Finset.mem_range.mp hb)))
        (congrArg Prod.fst eqcode)
    · exact sumCode_injective (congrArg Prod.snd eqcode)
  have card := Finset.card_le_card_of_injOn code (fun j _ => Finset.mem_univ (code j)) injective
  simp only [Finset.card_range, Finset.card_univ, Fintype.card_prod, Fintype.card_option,
    Fintype.card_fin, Fintype.card_pi, Finset.prod_const, Fintype.card_bool] at card
  rw [← pow_mul, Nat.mul_comm (2 * s + 1) N.k] at card
  convert card using 1
  simp only [configBound]
  ring

/-- No branch can accept before making a transition. [AB09, §4.1.1]

**Proof sketch.** The only zero-length choice word is empty, and the initial
configuration has a live control state. -/
theorem not_acceptsWithin_zero (N : FinNDTM Bool) (x : List Bool) :
    ¬ N.AcceptsWithin x 0 := by
  rintro ⟨w, hw, halted, _⟩
  have empty := List.length_eq_zero_iff.mp hw
  subst w
  simp at halted

/-- **Claim 4.4(1), acceptance form** (proved — phase P4.2): an
accepting branch of length `T` whose sibling branches of length `T` all stay
within `s` visited work cells shortens to an accepting branch of length the
vertex count: `AcceptsWithin x (N.configBound x.length s)`.

**Proof sketch.** Fix the accepting word `w`, `|w| = T`. Along its run every
head and nonblank cell stays in the window `[-s, s]` (the branch-space
hypothesis at `w` itself, through the interval structure of visited sets —
the `Turing.NDTM.visitedWith` analogues of `abs_pos_lt_card_visited` and
`mem_visited_of_ne_none`, named fill obligations). If two prefixes of the run
share a `Turing.NDTM.coreSum`, splice out the cycle: by
`Turing.NDTM.coreSum_stepWith` (iterated along the remaining choice bits) the
spliced run replays the suffix's vertices, so it halts with the same summary —
and `accept` as a final summary is acceptance, outputs being read only through
the summary. Iterate until all vertices along the branch are distinct; their
codes (`Turing.MultiTapeTM.ConfigCount.coreCode` within the window, paired
with the summary) are injective (`coreCode_inj`), so the branch length is at
most `N.configBound x.length s`, and the shortened word pads back up to the
exact count (`Turing.FinNDTM.AcceptsWithin.mono` — `AcceptsWithin` demands
exact word length); if the original `T` is already smaller, pad directly
instead (the same `mono`). In either case it is the **accepting branch**
that stays halted under padding (`Turing.NDTM.runWith_of_halt`): the
statement carries no sibling-halting hypothesis and needs none (round-1
audit, finding 1). -/
theorem acceptsWithin_of_spaceUsedWith_le (N : FinNDTM Bool) {x : List Bool}
    {T s : ℕ} (hacc : N.AcceptsWithin x T)
    (hs : ∀ w : List Bool, w.length = T →
      N.tm.spaceUsedWith w (N.tm.initCfg x) ≤ s) :
    N.AcceptsWithin x (N.configBound x.length s) := by
  classical
  by_cases short : T ≤ N.configBound x.length s
  · exact hacc.mono short
  obtain ⟨w, hw, halted, output⟩ := hacc
  -- Minimize among accepting words whose actual prefixes fit the coding window.
  let good (t : ℕ) : Prop := ∃ v : List Bool, v.length = t ∧
    (N.tm.runWith v (N.tm.initCfg x)).state = none ∧
    (N.tm.runWith v (N.tm.initCfg x)).output = [true] ∧
    ∀ j ≤ t, InWindow s (N.tm.runWith (v.take j) (N.tm.initCfg x))
  have exists_good : ∃ t, good t := ⟨T, w, hw, halted, output,
    fun j _ => NDTM.runWith_take_inWindow N.tm w (hs w hw) j⟩
  obtain ⟨v, hv, hvhalt, hvout, window⟩ := Nat.find_spec exists_good
  -- A repeated summary vertex produces a strictly shorter accepting word.
  have no_repeat (a b : ℕ) (ab : a < b) (bv : b ≤ v.length) :
      NDTM.coreSum (N.tm.runWith (v.take a) (N.tm.initCfg x)) ≠
        NDTM.coreSum (N.tm.runWith (v.take b) (N.tm.initCfg x)) := by
    intro same
    let u := v.take a ++ v.drop b
    obtain ⟨final, prefixes⟩ := NDTM.splice_vertices N.tm (N.tm.initCfg x) v ab.le bv same
    have shorter : u.length < Nat.find exists_good := by
      dsimp [u]
      rw [List.length_append, List.length_take_of_le (ab.le.trans bv), List.length_drop]
      omega
    have u_good : good u.length := by
      refine ⟨u, rfl, ?_, ?_, ?_⟩
      · exact (congrArg (fun vertex => vertex.1.1) final).trans hvhalt
      · apply (outSummary_eq_accept_iff _).mp
        exact (congrArg Prod.snd final).trans ((outSummary_eq_accept_iff _).mpr hvout)
      · intro j hj
        obtain ⟨l, hl, vertex⟩ := prefixes j hj
        exact NDTM.inWindow_of_coreSum_eq vertex (window l (hl.trans_eq hv))
    exact (Nat.not_le_of_lt shorter) (Nat.find_min' exists_good u_good)
  have distinct : Set.InjOn
      (fun j => NDTM.coreSum (N.tm.runWith (v.take j) (N.tm.initCfg x)))
      (Finset.range (Nat.find exists_good + 1)) := by
    intro a ha b hb same
    have a_bound := Nat.le_of_lt_succ (Finset.mem_range.mp ha)
    have b_bound := Nat.le_of_lt_succ (Finset.mem_range.mp hb)
    by_contra ne
    rcases Nat.lt_or_gt_of_ne ne with ab | ba
    · exact no_repeat a b ab (by omega) same
    · exact no_repeat b a ba (by omega) same.symm
  have count := count_windowed_vertices N x s (Nat.find exists_good)
    (fun j => N.tm.runWith (v.take j) (N.tm.initCfg x)) window distinct
  exact (show N.AcceptsWithin x (Nat.find exists_good) from ⟨v, hv, hvhalt, hvout⟩).mono
    (by omega)

/-- **The packaged graph interface** (proved — phase P4.2): a
machine deciding `L` in space `s` accepts exactly the members within the
vertex-count budget. This is the single statement the exponential-time
simulation ([AB09, Theorem 4.2]), `Complexity.NL_subset_P`, and Savitch's
midpoint recursion all consume.

**Proof sketch.** Forward: `Turing.FinNDTM.DecidesInSpace` supplies the budget
`T` with all-branch halting, the branch-space bound, and the acceptance
equivalence; `Turing.FinNDTM.acceptsWithin_of_spaceUsedWith_le` shortens to
the vertex count. Backward: given an accepting branch at the vertex-count
budget, compare with `T`: if the budget exceeds `T`, the branch's `T`-prefix
is already halted (`Turing.NDTM.HaltsWithin`) with the run frozen
(`Turing.NDTM.runWith_of_halt`), so the prefix accepts and membership follows
from the equivalence at `T`; otherwise pad
(`Turing.FinNDTM.AcceptsWithin.mono`). -/
theorem DecidesInSpace.mem_iff_acceptsWithin_configBound {N : FinNDTM Bool}
    {L : Language Bool} {s : ℕ → ℕ} (h : N.DecidesInSpace L s) (x : List Bool) :
    x ∈ L ↔ N.AcceptsWithin x (N.configBound x.length (s x.length)) := by
  obtain ⟨T, halt, space, iff_at_T⟩ := h x
  constructor
  · intro member
    exact acceptsWithin_of_spaceUsedWith_le N (iff_at_T.mp member) space
  · intro accepts
    apply iff_at_T.mpr
    by_cases budget : N.configBound x.length (s x.length) ≤ T
    · exact accepts.mono budget
    · obtain ⟨w, hw, _, output⟩ := accepts
      have prefix_length : (w.take T).length = T := List.length_take_of_le (by omega)
      have prefix_halt := halt (w.take T) prefix_length
      have frozen : N.tm.runWith w (N.tm.initCfg x) =
          N.tm.runWith (w.take T) (N.tm.initCfg x) := by
        conv_lhs => rw [← List.take_append_drop T w]
        rw [NDTM.runWith_append, NDTM.runWith_of_halt _ prefix_halt]
      exact ⟨w.take T, prefix_length, prefix_halt, by rw [← frozen]; exact output⟩

/-- The canonical rich record of a graph vertex, using S1a's summary code.
It records precisely the core and output summary, not the output history. -/
private def s1b_record (s : ℕ) (c : Cfg k Bool S x) : List (List (RecSym S (Fin 3))) :=
  cfgRecord s c (sumCode (outSummary c.output))

/-- Canonical records identify exactly S1a's vertices on the coding window.
This is the decoding part of the note-6 bridge, a Savitch promotion candidate.

**Proof sketch.** The received `cfgRecord_inj` recovers all four core fields
and the tag. S1a's injective `sumCode` recovers the output summary. -/
private theorem s1b_record_eq_iff {s : ℕ} {c d : Cfg k Bool S x}
    (hc : c.InWindow s) (hd : d.InWindow s) :
    s1b_record s c = s1b_record s d ↔ NDTM.coreSum c = NDTM.coreSum d := by
  rw [s1b_record, s1b_record, cfgRecord_inj s hc hd]
  simp only [NDTM.coreSum, MultiTapeTM.ConfigCount.core, Prod.mk.injEq,
    sumCode_injective.eq_iff]

/-- The quotient edge implemented by the two record-step calls. Requiring
the successor window is the semantic rejection of an outside-window step;
the received `exists_recordStepTM` supplies the machine's `no` branch. -/
private def s1b_recordEdge (tm : NDTM k Bool S) (s : ℕ)
    (fs gs : List (List (RecSym S (Fin 3)))) : Prop :=
  ∃ (c : Cfg k Bool S x) (b : Bool), c.InWindow s ∧ (tm.stepWith b c).InWindow s ∧
    fs = s1b_record s c ∧ gs = s1b_record s (tm.stepWith b c)

/-- Every path of canonical records lifts to a choice-word run from the
supplied actual configuration, in particular the true initial configuration.
The reflexive case uses the empty word. This is part of the note-6 promotion
candidate; it does not assert a table-machine invariant.

**Proof sketch.** At each quotient edge decode equality with its source,
apply S1a's `coreSum_stepWith`, and transfer window validity from the edge's
representative. Append that edge's bit to the actual run. -/
private theorem s1b_recordPath_lift (tm : NDTM k Bool S) {s : ℕ}
    {c : Cfg k Bool S x} (hc : c.InWindow s) {fs : List (List (RecSym S (Fin 3)))}
    (path : Relation.ReflTransGen (s1b_recordEdge (x := x) tm s) (s1b_record s c) fs) :
    ∃ w : List Bool, (tm.runWith w c).InWindow s ∧ s1b_record s (tm.runWith w c) = fs := by
  induction path with
  | refl => exact ⟨[], hc, rfl⟩
  | @tail fs gs _ edge ih =>
    obtain ⟨w, hw, hrecord⟩ := ih
    obtain ⟨d, b, hd, hnext, hfs, hgs⟩ := edge
    have same := (s1b_record_eq_iff hw hd).mp (hrecord.trans hfs)
    have next := NDTM.coreSum_stepWith tm b same
    have window : (tm.stepWith b (tm.runWith w c)).InWindow s :=
      (inWindow_iff_cfgInWindow _ _).mp
        (NDTM.inWindow_of_coreSum_eq next ((inWindow_iff_cfgInWindow _ _).mpr hnext))
    refine ⟨w ++ [b], ?_, ?_⟩
    · simpa only [NDTM.runWith_append, NDTM.runWith_cons, NDTM.runWith_nil] using window
    · simpa only [NDTM.runWith_append, NDTM.runWith_cons, NDTM.runWith_nil] using
        ((s1b_record_eq_iff window hnext).mpr next).trans hgs.symm

/-- A run whose prefixes stay in the window gives a path of canonical
records, including the zero-step path. This is the reverse direction of the
note-6 bridge, independent of a table representation.

**Proof sketch.** Each first bit gives one quotient edge; the remaining
prefixes are exactly the positive-length prefixes of the original word. -/
private theorem s1b_recordPath_of_run (tm : NDTM k Bool S) (s : ℕ) (w : List Bool)
    (c : Cfg k Bool S x) (hwindow : ∀ j, (tm.runWith (w.take j) c).InWindow s) :
    Relation.ReflTransGen (s1b_recordEdge (x := x) tm s)
      (s1b_record s c) (s1b_record s (tm.runWith w c)) := by
  induction w generalizing c with
  | nil => exact Relation.ReflTransGen.refl
  | cons b w ih =>
    have hc : c.InWindow s := by simpa using hwindow 0
    have hb : (tm.stepWith b c).InWindow s := by simpa using hwindow 1
    apply Relation.ReflTransGen.head ⟨c, b, hc, hb, rfl, rfl⟩
    apply ih
    intro j
    simpa only [List.take_succ_cons, NDTM.runWith_cons] using hwindow (j + 1)

/-- Representatives of the three summary codes, used only to compute tag
updates. The encoding itself is the received `sumCode`. -/
private def s1b_summaryWord (τ : Fin 3) : List Bool :=
  if τ = sumCode .empty then [] else if τ = sumCode .accept then [true] else [false]

/-- Each chosen representative has the requested summary code.

**Proof sketch.** Check the three elements of `Fin 3`; the existing encoding
computes on the empty, accepting and dead representative words. -/
private theorem s1b_summaryWord_code (τ : Fin 3) :
    sumCode (outSummary (s1b_summaryWord τ)) = τ := by
  fin_cases τ <;> rfl

/-- The record-step tag update is summary append on a representative word. -/
private def s1b_tagUpdate (τ : Fin 3) (b : Option Bool) : Fin 3 :=
  sumCode (outSummary (s1b_summaryWord τ ++ b.toList))

/-- An absent emission preserves the tag, as required by `recordStepTM`.

**Proof sketch.** Appending no symbol preserves the representative word. -/
private theorem s1b_tagUpdate_none (τ : Fin 3) : s1b_tagUpdate τ none = τ := by
  simpa [s1b_tagUpdate] using s1b_summaryWord_code τ

/-- The finite tag update agrees with every actual output history.

**Proof sketch.** The representative and actual word have equal summaries
by injectivity of S1a's code. Apply its append-congruence theorem. -/
private theorem s1b_tagUpdate_output (u : List Bool) (b : Option Bool) :
    s1b_tagUpdate (sumCode (outSummary u)) b = sumCode (outSummary (u ++ b.toList)) := by
  exact congrArg sumCode (outSummary_append_congr
    (sumCode_injective (s1b_summaryWord_code (sumCode (outSummary u)))) b.toList)

/-- The verdict is a predicate on every decoded record, with no distinguished
accepting vertex. Equality of records preserves it even when output histories
differ. [AB09, §4.1.1]

**Proof sketch.** A record's tag accepts precisely when the summary is
`accept`, by S1a's injective code; its summary accepts precisely `[true]`. -/
private theorem s1b_record_accepts (c : Cfg k Bool S x) :
    (c.state = none ∧ sumCode (outSummary c.output) = sumCode .accept) ↔
      c.Halted ∧ c.output = [true] := by
  rw [sumCode_injective.eq_iff, outSummary_eq_accept_iff]

end FinNDTM

end Turing

namespace Complexity

open Turing

/-- The configuration-count formula is exponential in any bound dominating
`logSpace`, with no monotonicity assumption. [AB09, Claim 4.4(1)]
This formula-level helper is a promotion candidate for Savitch.

**Proof sketch.** P4.2 Question 5 bounds the input factor by `2^(u+1)`,
the cell alphabet by `2^2`, and the head range by `2^(a*u+1)`.
Multiplication adds the exponents; the displayed coefficient absorbs their
constant terms and the finite state factor. -/
private theorem s1b_count_le_exp (q k a n u : ℕ) (hu : logSpace n ≤ u) :
    (q + 1) * (n + 2) * 3 ^ (k * (2 * (a * u) + 1)) * (2 * (a * u) + 1) ^ k ≤
      2 ^ ((q + 2 + k * (5 * a + 3)) * (u + 1)) := by
  have input : n + 2 ≤ 2 ^ (u + 1) := by
    have hn : n + 1 ≤ 2 ^ u :=
      (Nat.lt_pow_succ_log_self (by decide : 1 < 2) n).trans_le
        (Nat.pow_le_pow_right (by decide) hu)
    have hp : 0 < 2 ^ u := Nat.two_pow_pos u
    rw [pow_succ]
    omega
  have head : 2 * (a * u) + 1 ≤ 2 ^ (a * u + 1) := by
    have hp := Nat.lt_two_pow_self (n := a * u)
    rw [pow_succ]
    omega
  calc
    _ ≤ 2 ^ (q + 1) * 2 ^ (u + 1) *
        (2 ^ 2) ^ (k * (2 * (a * u) + 1)) * (2 ^ (a * u + 1)) ^ k :=
      Nat.mul_le_mul
        (Nat.mul_le_mul
          (Nat.mul_le_mul (Nat.le_of_lt (Nat.lt_two_pow_self (n := q + 1))) input)
          (Nat.pow_le_pow_left (by decide : 3 ≤ 2 ^ 2) _))
        (Nat.pow_le_pow_left head k)
    _ = 2 ^ ((q + 1) + (u + 1) + 2 * (k * (2 * (a * u) + 1)) + (a * u + 1) * k) := by
      simp only [← pow_mul, ← pow_add]
    _ ≤ _ := Nat.pow_le_pow_right (by decide) (by nlinarith)

/-- The formula-level bound instantiated for the deterministic constructor.

**Proof sketch.** Unfold only the received count definition and apply the
single generalized counting argument. -/
private theorem s1b_constructor_count (M : FinTM Bool) (a n u : ℕ)
    (hu : logSpace n ≤ u) :
    M.configBound n (a * u) ≤
      2 ^ ((Fintype.card M.State + 2 + M.k * (5 * a + 3)) * (u + 1)) :=
  s1b_count_le_exp (Fintype.card M.State) M.k a n u hu

/-- The same formula-level bound, including the three output summaries, for
the nondeterministic graph. [AB09, Claim 4.4(1)]

**Proof sketch.** The received vertex count is three times the core count.
Bound three by four and absorb the two extra exponent units into the fixed
coefficient. -/
private theorem s1b_vertex_count (N : FinNDTM Bool) (a n u : ℕ)
    (hu : logSpace n ≤ u) :
    N.configBound n (a * u) ≤
      2 ^ ((Fintype.card N.State + 4 + N.k * (5 * a + 3)) * (u + 1)) := by
  unfold FinNDTM.configBound
  calc
    _ ≤ 2 ^ 2 * 2 ^ ((Fintype.card N.State + 2 + N.k * (5 * a + 3)) * (u + 1)) :=
      Nat.mul_le_mul (by decide) (s1b_count_le_exp _ _ _ _ _ hu)
    _ = 2 ^ (2 + (Fintype.card N.State + 2 + N.k * (5 * a + 3)) * (u + 1)) :=
      (pow_add _ _ _).symm
    _ ≤ _ := Nat.pow_le_pow_right (by decide) (by nlinarith)

/-- Normalizing the space constant does not change the deciding machine or
any branch's halting budget. No monotonicity of the space function is needed.

**Proof sketch.** Choose the original constant itself as the exponent, since
`c ≤ 2^c`. Enlarge only the space inequality in each received witness. The
constructibility lower bound makes the binary radius word canonical. -/
private theorem s1b_normalize_radius {S : ℕ → ℕ} (hdom : ∀ n, logSpace n ≤ S n)
    {L : Language Bool} {N : FinNDTM Bool} {c : ℕ}
    (hN : N.DecidesInSpace L fun n => c * S n) :
    ∃ j : ℕ, c ≤ 2 ^ j ∧
      N.DecidesInSpace L (fun n => 2 ^ j * S n) ∧
      ∀ n, (2 ^ j * S n).bits = List.replicate j false ++ (S n).bits := by
  have hc : c ≤ 2 ^ c := Nat.le_of_lt (Nat.lt_two_pow_self (n := c))
  refine ⟨c, hc, ?_, ?_⟩
  · intro x
    obtain ⟨T, hhalt, hspace, hacc⟩ := hN x
    exact ⟨T, hhalt, fun w hw => (hspace w hw).trans (Nat.mul_le_mul_right _ hc), hacc⟩
  · intro n
    apply bits_two_pow_mul
    have := hdom n
    unfold logSpace at this
    omega

/-- The received deterministic count supplies the constructor's time bound.
This isolates the noncircular time ledger of the radius phase.

**Proof sketch.** Each space-constructor witness already halts. Apply
`ComputesInTime.of_spaceUsed_le` to its finite run, then the deterministic
instance of the generalized count. -/
private theorem s1b_constructor_time {S : ℕ → ℕ} (hdom : ∀ n, logSpace n ≤ S n)
    {M : FinTM Bool} {a : ℕ}
    (hM : M.ComputesInSpace (fun x => (S x.length).bits) fun n => a * S n) :
    ∀ x, M.ComputesInTime x (S x.length).bits (M.configBound x.length (a * S x.length)) ∧
      M.configBound x.length (a * S x.length) ≤
        2 ^ ((Fintype.card M.State + 2 + M.k * (5 * a + 3)) * (S x.length + 1)) := by
  intro x
  obtain ⟨t, ht, hs⟩ := hM x
  exact ⟨ht.of_spaceUsed_le hs, s1b_constructor_count M a x.length (S x.length) (hdom _)⟩

end Complexity
```

## ===== TCSlib/Complexity/SpaceComplexity/Logspace/ImmermanSzelepcsenyi.lean =====

```
/-
Copyright (c) 2026 Seyoon Ragavan. All rights reserved.
Released under Apache 2.0 license as described in the file LICENSE.
Authors: Seyoon Ragavan
-/
import TCSlib.Complexity.SpaceComplexity.Logspace.Path
import TCSlib.Complexity.SpaceComplexity.Constructible
import TCSlib.Complexity.SpaceComplexity.Logspace.ISCountGenCorrect

set_option maxHeartbeats 0
set_option relaxedAutoImplicit false
set_option autoImplicit false

/-!
# The Immerman-Szelepcsényi theorem

[AB09, §4.3.2, Theorem 4.20 and Corollary 4.21]: nondeterministic space is
closed under complement — `PATH-complement ∈ NL`, hence `NL = coNL`, and for
space-constructible `S` the same inductive counting gives
`NSPACE(S) = coNSPACE(S)`. Phase P4.4 of `AroraBarakChapters3-4Plan.md`.

## Design

* **No read-once certificate model is introduced.** [AB09] proves Theorem
  4.20 in the certificate view of `NL` (its §4.3.1, Definition 4.19 — a
  read-once certificate tape), which the plan defers. The campaign's
  binary-choice NDTM makes that view *native*: a choice word is consumed one
  bit per step and can never be re-read, so the book's certificates are
  exactly choice words and the inductive-counting verifier runs directly on
  `Turing.FinNDTM` — the deviation is a simplification, recorded here for
  the audit.
* The counting runs directly over the **configuration graph** of an arbitrary
  `NSPACE S` decider (`S ≥ logSpace`), whose vertices are the codes of
  `TCSlib.Complexity.SpaceComplexity.Codec`: the generic
  `Complexity.compl_mem_NSPACE` (`L ∈ NSPACE S → Lᶜ ∈ NSPACE S`,
  `TCSlib.Complexity.SpaceComplexity.Logspace.ISCountGenCorrect`) is proved by the
  window-growing inductive-counting nondeterministic register machine
  `Complexity.LogProg.ISGen.igA`, and `Complexity.compl_mem_NL` is its case
  `S = logSpace` (`NL = NSPACE logSpace`). The `PATH` form is then a corollary of
  `Complexity.PATH_mem_NL`, and no `NL`-completeness of `PATH` or closure of
  `NL` under logspace reductions is needed.

## Main results

* `Complexity.compl_PATH_mem_NL` — [AB09, Theorem 4.20] as stated there.
* `Complexity.NL_eq_coNL` — the headline equality. [AB09, §4.3.2]
* `Complexity.NSPACE_compl_eq` — [AB09, Corollary 4.21], from the generic
  `Complexity.compl_mem_NSPACE` (`L ∈ NSPACE S → Lᶜ ∈ NSPACE S` for `S ≥ log`,
  `TCSlib.Complexity.SpaceComplexity.Logspace.ISCountGenCorrect`), proved by a
  window-growing variant of the counting machine that finds the window radius
  itself; of `SpaceConstructible S` only the conjunct `S ≥ logSpace` is used.

## References

* [AB09] S. Arora, B. Barak, *Computational Complexity: A Modern Approach*,
  Cambridge University Press, 2009. (§4.3.1-§4.3.2, Theorem 4.20,
  Corollary 4.21.)
* [Imm88] N. Immerman, *Nondeterministic space is closed under
  complementation*, SIAM J. Comput. 17(5), 1988; [Sze87] R. Szelepcsényi,
  *The method of forcing for nondeterministic automata*, Acta Informatica
  26, 1988. (Cited through [AB09]; no external text required.)
-/

namespace Complexity

open Turing

/-- **`PATH`-complement is in `NL`** ([AB09, Theorem 4.20]): nonreachability has
nondeterministically verifiable certificates, by inductive counting.

**Proof sketch.** `PATH ∈ NL` (`Complexity.PATH_mem_NL`), and `NL` is closed under
complement (`Complexity.compl_mem_NL`, the case `S = logSpace` of
`Complexity.compl_mem_NSPACE`): the window-growing inductive-counting register machine runs
on the configuration graph of the `PATH` walk machine, at radii `s = 0, 1, …`, computing for
`i = 0, …, K - 1` the size of the ball `C_{i+1}` of codes reachable from the initial code
within `i + 1` steps from the size `cp` of `C_i`. Every code `v` is guessed in or out of
`C_{i+1}` in ascending order; a member is certified by a guessed walk (and must not be
accepting); a non-member by enumerating, again in ascending order, exactly `cp` guessed
members of `C_i` with their walks, none equal to `v` or stepping to `v`. It stops at the
first radius whose count of reachable codes equals the previous one. Choice words serve as
the certificates (native read-once). All registers have `O(log |x|)` digits and every branch
halts. -/
theorem compl_PATH_mem_NL : (PATHᶜ : Language Bool) ∈ NL := by
  exact compl_mem_NL PATH_mem_NL

/-- **`NL = coNL`** ([AB09, §4.3.2]).

**Proof sketch.** Both inclusions are `Complexity.compl_mem_NL`, i.e.
`Complexity.compl_mem_NSPACE` at `S = logSpace` (inductive counting on the configuration
graph of an `NL` decider): `L ∈ NL` gives `Lᶜ ∈ NL`, i.e. `L ∈ coNL`; and `Lᶜ ∈ NL` gives
`Lᶜᶜ = L ∈ NL` (complements are involutive). -/
theorem NL_eq_coNL : NL = coNL := by
  ext L
  exact ⟨fun h => compl_mem_NL h, fun h => compl_compl L ▸ compl_mem_NL h⟩

/-- **Nondeterministic space is closed under complement**
([AB09, Corollary 4.21]): for space-constructible `S`, the complements of
`NSPACE S` languages are exactly `NSPACE S`.

**Proof sketch.** Both inclusions are `Complexity.compl_mem_NSPACE` (with
`S ≥ logSpace`, the first conjunct of `Complexity.SpaceConstructible`) and the
involution `Lᶜᶜ = L`. `compl_mem_NSPACE` runs the inductive counting of
`Complexity.compl_PATH_mem_NL` on the configuration graph of a decider `N` of
`L` in space `c · S` (codes of window-bounded configurations, membership
certificates guessed walks of step pairs), but does **not** compute the window
radius from the constructibility witness as [AB09, Exercise 4.11] suggests:
the window-growing machine `Complexity.LogProg.ISGen.igA` counts the reachable
codes at radii `s = 0, 1, …` and stops at the first radius whose count equals
the previous one — the window is then closed under steps, so acceptance is
decided by the reachable codes (`Complexity.ExpBFS.mem_iff_of_card_eq`); the
counts agree above `c · S |x|` (`Complexity.ExpBFS.card_rset_succ_of_le`), so
the radius stays at most `c · S |x| + 1` and all registers have `O(S |x|)`
digits, within `Complexity.LogProg.narm_decides_space` with logspace code
deciders. -/
theorem NSPACE_compl_eq (S : ℕ → ℕ) (hS : SpaceConstructible S) :
    {L : Language Bool | Lᶜ ∈ NSPACE S} = NSPACE S := by
  ext L
  exact ⟨fun h => compl_compl L ▸ compl_mem_NSPACE hS.1 h, fun h => compl_mem_NSPACE hS.1 h⟩

end Complexity
```

## ===== TCSlib/Complexity/SpaceComplexity/Logspace/Path.lean =====

```
/-
Copyright (c) 2026 Seyoon Ragavan. All rights reserved.
Released under Apache 2.0 license as described in the file LICENSE.
Authors: Seyoon Ragavan
-/
import Mathlib.Logic.Relation
import TCSlib.Complexity.SpaceComplexity.Logspace.Reductions
import TCSlib.Complexity.SpaceComplexity.ConfigGraph
import TCSlib.Complexity.SpaceComplexity.Logspace.PathWalkProof
import TCSlib.Complexity.SpaceComplexity.Logspace.PathHardDecide

set_option maxHeartbeats 0
set_option relaxedAutoImplicit false
set_option autoImplicit false

/-!
# The language `PATH` and its `NL`-completeness

[AB09, §4.1.2 and §4.3, (4.1) and Theorem 4.18]: directed `s`-`t`
connectivity is the language capturing nondeterministic logarithmic space.
Phase P4.4 of `AroraBarakChapters3-4Plan.md` — the campaign's first graph
encoding.

## Design

* **The encoding** `⟨G, s, t⟩` is
  `pairEncode 1ⁿ (pairEncode (row-major adjacency bits) (pairEncode (bits s) (bits t)))`:
  the unary vertex count makes `n` recoverable by a prefix scan, the matrix
  length is checkable as `n²`, and the endpoints ride in binary. Membership
  is by existential witness over genuine encodings (the `EXPCOM`/`dblLang`
  house pattern), so no total decode is needed; non-encodings are out of
  `PATH`.
* **Reachability is in-house**: `Complexity.GraphReach`, the reflexive-
  transitive closure of the decoded adjacency relation on `Fin n`. The plan
  (§2.6) named `GraphTheory`'s `Digraph.Reachable` as the semantic target;
  that tree currently carries admissions outside the audited closure, so the
  campaign keeps the relation local and records the bridging lemma as future
  work (plan decision log, this phase's row) — a deviation declared for the
  audit.

## Main definitions

* `Complexity.GraphReach` — reachability of the adjacency relation.
* `Complexity.encodePATH`, `Complexity.PATH` — the instance encoding and the
  language. [AB09, (4.1)]

## Main results (phase-P4.4 statements)

* `Complexity.PATH_mem_NL` — the nondeterministic walk (proved, by the
  nondeterministic register machine of `Logspace.PathWalk`). [AB09, Example 4.7,
  the `PATH ∈ NL` paragraph]
* `Complexity.PATH_NLComplete` — [AB09, Theorem 4.18] (proved: hardness by the
  configuration-graph reduction of `Logspace.PathHard`).

## References

* [AB09] S. Arora, B. Barak, *Computational Complexity: A Modern Approach*,
  Cambridge University Press, 2009. (§4.1.2, (4.1); §4.3, Theorem 4.18.)
-/

namespace Complexity

open Turing

/-- Reachability of the adjacency relation `A` on `Fin n`: the reflexive-
transitive closure of its edge relation. (In-house; the bridge to
`GraphTheory`'s digraph reachability is recorded future work — see the
module docstring.) -/
def GraphReach {n : ℕ} (A : Fin n → Fin n → Bool) (s t : Fin n) : Prop :=
  Relation.ReflTransGen (fun u v => A u v = true) s t

/-- **The `⟨G, s, t⟩` instance encoding**: unary vertex count, row-major
adjacency matrix, endpoints in binary — each layer an aligned pair, per the
campaign pairing. -/
def encodePATH (n : ℕ) (A : Fin n → Fin n → Bool) (s t : Fin n) : List Bool :=
  pairEncode (List.replicate n true)
    (pairEncode ((List.finRange n).flatMap fun u => (List.finRange n).map (A u))
      (pairEncode (Nat.bits (s : ℕ)) (Nat.bits (t : ℕ))))

/-- **The language `PATH`** [AB09, (4.1)]: encodings of directed graphs with
two designated vertices such that the second is reachable from the first.
Membership is by existential witness over genuine encodings; strings that
encode no instance are not in `PATH`. -/
def PATH : Language Bool :=
  {x | ∃ (n : ℕ) (A : Fin n → Fin n → Bool) (s t : Fin n),
    x = encodePATH n A s t ∧ GraphReach A s t}

/-- The row-major adjacency word of `encodePATH` has `n²` bits. -/
lemma length_adjWord (n : ℕ) (A : Fin n → Fin n → Bool) :
    ((List.finRange n).flatMap fun u => (List.finRange n).map (A u)).length = n * n := by
  simp [List.length_flatMap, List.sum_replicate]

/-- Reading a concatenation of rows of equal length `k` at row `i`, column `j`. -/
lemma getD_flatMap_rows {α : Type} (L : List α) (f : α → List Bool) (k : ℕ)
    (hf : ∀ a, (f a).length = k) (i j : ℕ) (hi : i < L.length) (hj : j < k) :
    (L.flatMap f).getD (i * k + j) false = (f L[i]).getD j false := by
  induction L generalizing i with
  | nil => simp at hi
  | cons a L ih =>
    rw [List.flatMap_cons]
    cases i with
    | zero =>
      simp only [Nat.zero_mul, Nat.zero_add, List.getElem_cons_zero]
      rw [List.getD_eq_getElem?_getD, List.getElem?_append_left (by rw [hf]; exact hj),
        ← List.getD_eq_getElem?_getD]
    | succ i =>
      simp only [List.getElem_cons_succ]
      have e : (i + 1) * k + j = k + (i * k + j) := by rw [Nat.add_mul, Nat.one_mul]; omega
      rw [e, List.getD_eq_getElem?_getD, List.getElem?_append_right (by rw [hf]; omega), hf,
        show k + (i * k + j) - k = i * k + j by omega, ← List.getD_eq_getElem?_getD]
      exact ih i (by simpa using hi)

/-- The bit of the row-major adjacency word at `u · n + v` is the edge bit `A u v`. -/
lemma adjWord_getD {n : ℕ} (A : Fin n → Fin n → Bool) (u v : Fin n) :
    ((List.finRange n).flatMap fun u => (List.finRange n).map (A u)).getD
      (u * n + v) false = A u v := by
  rw [getD_flatMap_rows _ _ n (fun _ => by simp) u v (by simp) v.isLt]
  simp [List.getD_eq_getElem?_getD]

/-- **`PATH` is the raw `PATH` language** of `Logspace.PathWalk`: the instance encoding
is the raw format with the row-major adjacency word, and graph reachability is
reachability along the word's edge relation below `n`.

**Proof sketch.** Forwards, lift the path along `Fin.val` (`adjWord_getD`). Backwards,
read the matrix off the word (`A u v = M[u · n + v]`); the word is then the adjacency word
of `A` (every index below `n²` is `(i / n) · n + i % n`), and a path of the word's edge
relation stays below `n`, so it is a path of `A`. -/
theorem PATH_eq_pathRawLang : PATH = pathRawLang := by
  ext x
  constructor
  · rintro ⟨n, A, s, t, hx, hr⟩
    refine ⟨n, _, s, t, length_adjWord n A, s.isLt, t.isLt, hx, ?_⟩
    exact Relation.ReflTransGen.lift Fin.val
      (fun a b h => ⟨a.isLt, b.isLt, by rw [adjWord_getD]; exact h⟩) hr
  · rintro ⟨n, M, s, t, hM, hs, ht, hx, hr⟩
    let A : Fin n → Fin n → Bool := fun u v => M.getD (u * n + v) false
    have hAM : ((List.finRange n).flatMap fun u => (List.finRange n).map (A u)) = M := by
      refine ext_getD' (by rw [length_adjWord, hM]) fun i hi => ?_
      rw [length_adjWord] at hi
      have hn : 0 < n := by
        rcases Nat.eq_zero_or_pos n with h | h
        · rw [h] at hi; simp at hi
        · exact h
      have hq : i / n < n := Nat.div_lt_of_lt_mul hi
      have hr' : i % n < n := Nat.mod_lt i hn
      have he : i = (i / n) * n + i % n := by rw [Nat.mul_comm]; exact (Nat.div_add_mod i n).symm
      have := adjWord_getD A ⟨i / n, hq⟩ ⟨i % n, hr'⟩
      simp only at this
      rw [← he] at this
      rw [this]
      simp only [A]
      rw [← he]
    refine ⟨n, A, ⟨s, hs⟩, ⟨t, ht⟩, by rw [hx, ← hAM]; rfl, ?_⟩
    have key : ∀ a, Relation.ReflTransGen (rawEdge n M) a t → ∀ ha : a < n,
        GraphReach A ⟨a, ha⟩ ⟨t, ht⟩ := by
      intro a h
      induction h using Relation.ReflTransGen.head_induction_on with
      | refl => intro _; exact Relation.ReflTransGen.refl
      | head hac _ ih =>
        intro ha
        exact Relation.ReflTransGen.head hac.2.2 (ih hac.2.1)
    exact key s hr hs

/-- **`PATH ∈ NL`** ([AB09, §4.1.2, the nondeterministic walk]): guess the path vertex by
vertex, keeping only the current vertex and a step counter.

**Proof sketch.** `PATH` is the raw language `pathRawLang` (`PATH_eq_pathRawLang`), which
the nondeterministic register machine `Complexity.LogProg.pathA` decides
(`Complexity.pathRawLang_mem_NL`, by `Complexity.LogProg.narm_decides_poly`). Reading the
input through the logspace bit and length deciders, the machine checks the unary prefix
`1ⁿ` and the shape of the `n²`-pair matrix field, guesses `s < n` and `t < n` and checks
them against the endpoint fields, then walks from `s`: if the current vertex is `t` it
accepts, after `n` steps it rejects, otherwise it guesses the next vertex `v < n`, computes
the position of the bit `A u v` by additions, rejects on a `0`, and moves to `v`. Every
branch halts and every register stays at most `4 (|x| + 1)`; some branch accepts iff `t` is
reachable from `s` within `n` edges, which by path shortening (`Complexity.reach_iff_walkLe`)
is reachability. -/
theorem PATH_mem_NL : PATH ∈ NL := by
  rw [PATH_eq_pathRawLang]
  exact pathRawLang_mem_NL

/-- **`PATH` is `NL`-complete** ([AB09, Theorem 4.18]): membership is
`Complexity.PATH_mem_NL`; hardness maps a language's machine-and-input to its configuration
graph.

**Proof sketch.** Membership is `PATH_mem_NL`. For hardness, `PATH` is the raw language
`pathRawLang` (`PATH_eq_pathRawLang`), and every `B ∈ NL` reduces to it
(`Complexity.pathRawLang_NLHard`): if `N` decides `B` in space `c₀ · logSpace`, the
reduction `Complexity.PathHard.red N c₀` sends `x` to the graph on `n = 2 ^ E` vertices
(`E = K (c₀ + 1) ℓ + K + 2`, `ℓ = |bits (|x| + 1)|`, `K = codeK N`, so `n` is polynomial in
`|x|`) whose vertex `c + 2` is the configuration code `c` at radius `s = c₀ ℓ`, with a
source `0` joined to the initial codes, a target `1` joined from the accepting codes, and the
step pairs of the codec as the remaining edges. Then `x ∈ B` iff `1` is reachable from `0`
(`PathHard.red_mem_iff`, from the bridge lemma `Complexity.Codec.mem_iff_codeChain` and
`Complexity.Codec.mem_of_codePath`); no accepting normalization of `N` is needed, since the
target collects all accepting codes. The reduction is implicitly logspace computable
(`PathHard.implicitlyLogspaceComputable_red`): its length `2n² + 2n + 7` is polynomial, and
a register machine (`PathHard.A`) answers a bit or length query `⟨x, bits i⟩` by parsing the
query, computing `E` and the block lengths by counting loops, decoding `i`, locating it in
the layout (unary block, separator, doubled adjacency word, tail) by comparisons and
subtractions, splitting a matrix offset into a vertex pair by halving and shifting, and
asking the logspace initial-, accepting- or step-code decider of the codec (read through
`Complexity.dropIdx`); `Complexity.LogProg.arm_decides_poly` turns it into a logspace
decider. -/
theorem PATH_NLComplete : NLComplete PATH := by
  refine ⟨PATH_mem_NL, fun B hB => ?_⟩
  rw [PATH_eq_pathRawLang]
  exact pathRawLang_NLHard hB

end Complexity
```

## ===== TCSlib/Complexity/SpaceComplexity/Machines/Compile.lean =====

```
/-
Copyright (c) 2026 TCSlib contributors. All rights reserved.
Released under Apache 2.0 license as described in the file LICENSE.
Authors: Hydroxyi
-/
import Mathlib.Algebra.BigOperators.Fin
import TCSlib.Complexity.SpaceComplexity.Machines.Call

set_option maxHeartbeats 0
set_option relaxedAutoImplicit false
set_option autoImplicit false

/-!
# Correctness of the compiled machine

The semantics of a register-tape program (`Complexity.LogProg.rstep`): ordinary nodes take
their machine step, a call node asks an oracle about the virtual input of the call
(`Complexity.LogProg.vword` of `Complexity.LogProg.callSegs`) and continues in its `yes` or
`no` state with the input head back on the first cell. If the deciders answer the oracle
cleanly, the compiled machine (`Complexity.LogProg.compileTM`) computes what the program
computes (`Complexity.LogProg.compile_correct`), in space bounded by the program's register
ranges plus the deciders' space (`Complexity.LogProg.compile_space`).

## Main definitions

* `Complexity.LogProg.tapeWord` — the word stored on a register tape.
* `Complexity.LogProg.rstep` — one step of a program, calls being atomic oracle questions.
* `Complexity.LogProg.CallOK` — the precondition of one call, required at every step
  along the run by the compilation theorems' `hcalls` hypotheses.
* `Complexity.LogProg.compileFinTM` — the compiled machine as a bundled finite machine.

## Main results

* `Complexity.LogProg.compile_correct` — the compiled machine halts with the program's
  output, all heads in the given ranges at all times; `compile_correct_from` is its form
  from an arbitrary program configuration.
* `Complexity.LogProg.compile_space` — its space usage is at most the sum of the register
  ranges plus `kD (2B + 1)`.

## References

* [AB09] S. Arora, B. Barak, *Computational Complexity: A Modern Approach*,
  Cambridge University Press, 2009. (§4.3, proof of Lemma 4.17.)
-/

namespace Complexity.LogProg

open Turing

variable {m d kD : ℕ} {Λ SD : Type} {x : List Bool}

/-- The word stored on a register tape (from cell `0`; `[]` if the tape is not of this
shape). -/
noncomputable def tapeWord (f : ℤ → Option Bool) : List Bool :=
  open Classical in if h : ∃ w, f = FinTM.bufferTape w then h.choose else []

/-- A stored word is read back. -/
lemma tapeWord_bufferTape (w : List Bool) : tapeWord (FinTM.bufferTape w) = w := by
  have h : ∃ w', FinTM.bufferTape w = FinTM.bufferTape w' := ⟨w, rfl⟩
  unfold tapeWord
  rw [dif_pos h]
  have hspec := h.choose_spec
  -- `bufferTape` is injective
  apply List.ext_getElem?
  intro i
  have := congrFun hspec (i : ℤ)
  simpa [FinTM.bufferTape] using this.symm

/-- The register words of a program configuration. -/
noncomputable def regWords (c : Cfg m Bool Λ x) (r : Fin m) : List Bool := tapeWord (c.workTapes r)

/-- **One step of a register-tape program**: an ordinary node takes its machine step; a call
node asks `oracle` (decider `cs.dec`) about its virtual input and moves to `yes` or `no`,
with the input head on the first cell. -/
noncomputable def rstep (P : RProg m d Λ) (oracle : Fin d → List Bool → Bool)
    (c : Cfg m Bool Λ x) : Cfg m Bool Λ x :=
  match c.state with
  | none => c
  | some l =>
    match P.call l with
    | none => P.tm.step c
    | some cs =>
      { c with
        state := some (if oracle cs.dec (vword (callSegs cs x (regWords c))) then cs.yes
          else cs.no),
        inputPos := 1 }

/-- The program run: `n` steps of `rstep`. -/
noncomputable def rrun (P : RProg m d Λ) (oracle : Fin d → List Bool → Bool)
    (c : Cfg m Bool Λ x) (n : ℕ) : Cfg m Bool Λ x :=
  (rstep P oracle)^[n] c

/-- Running a register-tape program `n + 1` steps is one more step after `n` steps. -/
lemma rrun_succ (P : RProg m d Λ) (oracle : Fin d → List Bool → Bool) (c : Cfg m Bool Λ x)
    (n : ℕ) : rrun P oracle c (n + 1) = rstep P oracle (rrun P oracle c n) := by
  simp [rrun, Function.iterate_succ_apply']

/-- The preconditions of a call at configuration `c` (if `c` is at a call node): distinct
argument registers holding words with their heads at the origin and within the register
ranges, input head on the first cell, and a decider answering the oracle cleanly within head
range `B`. -/
def CallOK (P : RProg m d Λ) (D : MultiTapeTM kD Bool SD) (q0 : Fin d → SD)
    (oracle : Fin d → List Bool → Bool) (lo hi : Fin m → ℤ) (B : ℕ) (c : Cfg m Bool Λ x) :
    Prop :=
  ∀ l cs, c.state = some l → P.call l = some cs →
    cs.args.Nodup ∧ c.inputPos.val = 1 ∧
    (∀ r ∈ cs.args, c.workTapes r = FinTM.bufferTape (regWords c r) ∧ c.workTapePos r = 0 ∧
      lo r ≤ -1 ∧ ((regWords c r).length : ℤ) ≤ hi r) ∧
    CleanRun D (q0 cs.dec) (vword (callSegs cs x (regWords c)))
      (oracle cs.dec (vword (callSegs cs x (regWords c)))) B

/-- **Correctness of the compiled machine, from any program configuration.** If the program
runs `N` steps from `c`, its register heads stay in `[lo r, hi r]`, and every call along the
way meets its preconditions, then the compiled machine, started on the seam of `c`, reaches
the seam of the program configuration after `N` steps, and at every time its register heads
are in `[lo r, hi r]` and its decider heads in `[-B, B]`. (`compile_correct` is the case of
the initial configuration; the general form is used to splice compiled runs between
nondeterministic choices.)

**Proof sketch.** Induction on the program run, keeping the compiled machine on the seam
(`Complexity.LogProg.seam`) of the program configuration: ordinary steps are simulated in
lockstep (`step_seam_prog`), calls by `call_run`. -/
theorem compile_correct_from (P : RProg m d Λ) (l₀ : Λ) (D : MultiTapeTM kD Bool SD)
    (q0 : Fin d → SD) (oracle : Fin d → List Bool → Bool) (lo hi : Fin m → ℤ) (B : ℕ)
    (c₀ : Cfg m Bool Λ x) (N : ℕ)
    (hbox : ∀ t ≤ N, ∀ r, lo r ≤ (rrun P oracle c₀ t).workTapePos r ∧
      (rrun P oracle c₀ t).workTapePos r ≤ hi r)
    (hcalls : ∀ t < N, CallOK P D q0 oracle lo hi B (rrun P oracle c₀ t)) :
    ∃ T, (compileTM P l₀ D q0).runFrom (seam c₀) T = seam (rrun P oracle c₀ N) ∧
      ∀ t ≤ T, (∀ r, lo r ≤ ((compileTM P l₀ D q0).runFrom (seam c₀)
          t).workTapePos (Fin.castAdd kD r) ∧
          ((compileTM P l₀ D q0).runFrom (seam c₀) t).workTapePos
            (Fin.castAdd kD r) ≤ hi r) ∧
        ∀ i, |((compileTM P l₀ D q0).runFrom (seam c₀) t).workTapePos
          (Fin.natAdd m i)| ≤ B := by
  induction N with
  | zero =>
    refine ⟨0, by rw [MultiTapeTM.runFrom_zero]; rfl, fun t ht => ?_⟩
    obtain rfl : t = 0 := by omega
    refine ⟨fun r => ?_, fun i => ?_⟩
    · have := hbox 0 le_rfl r
      simpa [seam, rrun] using this
    · simp [seam]
  | succ N ih =>
    obtain ⟨T, hT, hTb⟩ := ih (fun t ht => hbox t (by omega)) (fun t ht => hcalls t (by omega))
    set c := rrun P oracle c₀ N with hc
    have hbN := hbox N (by omega)
    have hbN1 := hbox (N + 1) le_rfl
    rw [rrun_succ, ← hc] at hbN1 ⊢
    -- one program step from `c`
    have hstep : ∃ T', (compileTM P l₀ D q0).runFrom (seam c) T' = seam (rstep P oracle c) ∧
        ∀ t ≤ T', (∀ r, lo r ≤ ((compileTM P l₀ D q0).runFrom (seam c) t).workTapePos
            (Fin.castAdd kD r) ∧ ((compileTM P l₀ D q0).runFrom (seam c) t).workTapePos
              (Fin.castAdd kD r) ≤ hi r) ∧
          ∀ i, |((compileTM P l₀ D q0).runFrom (seam c) t).workTapePos (Fin.natAdd m i)| ≤ B := by
      cases hs : c.state with
      | none =>
        refine ⟨0, by simp [rstep, hs], fun t ht => ?_⟩
        obtain rfl : t = 0 := by omega
        exact ⟨fun r => by simpa [seam] using hbN r, fun i => by simp [seam]⟩
      | some l =>
        cases hcl : P.call l with
        | none =>
          have hst := step_seam_prog P l₀ D q0 c l hs hcl
          have hr : rstep P oracle c = P.tm.step c := by simp [rstep, hs, hcl]
          refine ⟨1, by rw [hr]; exact hst, fun t ht => ?_⟩
          rcases Nat.lt_or_ge t 1 with h | h
          · obtain rfl : t = 0 := by omega
            exact ⟨fun r => by simpa [seam] using hbN r, fun i => by simp [seam]⟩
          · obtain rfl : t = 1 := by omega
            rw [show (compileTM P l₀ D q0).runFrom (seam c) 1 =
              (compileTM P l₀ D q0).step (seam c) from rfl, hst, ← hr]
            exact ⟨fun r => by simpa [seam] using hbN1 r, fun i => by simp [seam]⟩
        | some cs =>
          obtain ⟨hnd, hin, hargs, hclean⟩ := hcalls N (by omega) l cs hs hcl
          obtain ⟨T', hb', hr'⟩ := call_run P l₀ D q0 hs hcl (fun r hr => (hargs r hr).1)
            (fun r hr => (hargs r hr).2.1) hnd hin _ B hclean
          have hr : rstep P oracle c = { c with
              state := some (if oracle cs.dec (vword (callSegs cs x (regWords c))) then cs.yes
                else cs.no), inputPos := 1 } := by simp [rstep, hs, hcl]
          refine ⟨T', by rw [hr]; exact hr', fun t ht => ⟨fun r => ?_, (hb' t ht).2⟩⟩
          obtain ⟨h1, h2⟩ := (hb' t ht).1 r
          beta_reduce at h1 h2
          by_cases hrm : r ∈ cs.args
          · obtain ⟨-, -, hlo, hhi⟩ := hargs r hrm
            have := h2 hrm
            constructor <;> omega
          · rw [h1 hrm]; exact hbN r
    obtain ⟨T', hT', hTb'⟩ := hstep
    refine ⟨T + T', by rw [MultiTapeTM.runFrom_add, hT, hT'], ?_⟩
    apply runFrom_forall_append (Q := fun g =>
      (∀ r, lo r ≤ g.workTapePos (Fin.castAdd kD r) ∧ g.workTapePos (Fin.castAdd kD r) ≤ hi r) ∧
        ∀ i, |g.workTapePos (Fin.natAdd m i)| ≤ B) hTb
    rw [hT]
    exact hTb'


/-- **Correctness of the compiled machine.** If the program halts after `N` steps with
output `w`, its register heads stay in `[lo r, hi r]`, and every call along the way meets
its preconditions, then the compiled machine halts with output `w`, and at every time its
register heads are in `[lo r, hi r]` and its decider heads in `[-B, B]`.

**Proof sketch.** Induction on the program run, keeping the compiled machine on the seam
(`Complexity.LogProg.seam`) of the program configuration: ordinary steps are simulated in
lockstep (`step_seam_prog`), calls by `call_run`. -/
theorem compile_correct (P : RProg m d Λ) (l₀ : Λ) (D : MultiTapeTM kD Bool SD)
    (q0 : Fin d → SD) (oracle : Fin d → List Bool → Bool) (lo hi : Fin m → ℤ) (B : ℕ)
    (N : ℕ)
    (hbox : ∀ t ≤ N, ∀ r, lo r ≤ (rrun P oracle (Cfg.init l₀ x) t).workTapePos r ∧
      (rrun P oracle (Cfg.init l₀ x) t).workTapePos r ≤ hi r)
    (hcalls : ∀ t < N, CallOK P D q0 oracle lo hi B (rrun P oracle (Cfg.init l₀ x) t)) :
    ∃ T, (compileTM P l₀ D q0).runFrom ((compileTM P l₀ D q0).initCfg x) T =
        seam (rrun P oracle (Cfg.init l₀ x) N) ∧
      ∀ t ≤ T, (∀ r, lo r ≤ ((compileTM P l₀ D q0).runFrom ((compileTM P l₀ D q0).initCfg x)
          t).workTapePos (Fin.castAdd kD r) ∧
          ((compileTM P l₀ D q0).runFrom ((compileTM P l₀ D q0).initCfg x) t).workTapePos
            (Fin.castAdd kD r) ≤ hi r) ∧
        ∀ i, |((compileTM P l₀ D q0).runFrom ((compileTM P l₀ D q0).initCfg x) t).workTapePos
          (Fin.natAdd m i)| ≤ B := by
  have h := compile_correct_from P l₀ D q0 oracle lo hi B (Cfg.init l₀ x) N hbox hcalls
  rw [seam_init]
  exact h

/-- The space used up to time `T` is bounded by the sizes of ranges containing every head
at every time up to `T`. -/
lemma spaceUsed_le_of_ranges {K : ℕ} {S : Type} (tm : MultiTapeTM K Bool S)
    (c : Cfg K Bool S x) (T : ℕ) (lo hi : Fin K → ℤ)
    (h : ∀ t ≤ T, ∀ i, lo i ≤ (tm.runFrom c t).workTapePos i ∧
      (tm.runFrom c t).workTapePos i ≤ hi i) :
    tm.spaceUsed c T ≤ ∑ i, (hi i - lo i + 1).toNat := by
  unfold MultiTapeTM.spaceUsed MultiTapeTM.spaceUsedByTape
  refine Finset.sum_le_sum fun i _ => ?_
  have hsub : tm.visitedByTapeHead c T i ⊆ Finset.Icc (lo i) (hi i) := by
    intro z hz
    simp only [MultiTapeTM.visitedByTapeHead, Finset.mem_image, Finset.mem_range] at hz
    obtain ⟨t, ht, rfl⟩ := hz
    rw [Finset.mem_Icc]
    exact h t (by omega) i
  refine (Finset.card_le_card hsub).trans (le_of_eq ?_)
  rw [Int.card_Icc]
  congr 1
  ring

/-- The compiled machine as a bundled finite machine. -/
def compileFinTM [Fintype Λ] [DecidableEq Λ] [Fintype SD] [DecidableEq SD]
    (P : RProg m d Λ) (l₀ : Λ) (D : MultiTapeTM kD Bool SD) (q0 : Fin d → SD) : FinTM Bool where
  k := m + kD
  State := CSt Λ SD m
  tm := compileTM P l₀ D q0

/-- **The compiled machine computes what the program computes, in the program's space plus
the deciders' space**: if the program halts after `N` steps with output `w`, register heads
in `[lo r, hi r]`, and all calls meet their preconditions with decider head range `B`, then
the compiled machine halts on `x` with output `w`, having visited at most
`∑ r (hi r - lo r + 1) + kD (2B + 1)` work cells.

**Proof sketch.** `compile_correct` gives the halting time and the head ranges;
`spaceUsed_le_of_ranges` turns ranges into space, the register tapes and the decider tapes
being the two blocks of `Fin (m + kD)`. -/
theorem compile_space [Fintype Λ] [DecidableEq Λ] [Fintype SD] [DecidableEq SD]
    (P : RProg m d Λ) (l₀ : Λ) (D : MultiTapeTM kD Bool SD) (q0 : Fin d → SD)
    (oracle : Fin d → List Bool → Bool) (lo hi : Fin m → ℤ) (B N : ℕ) (w : List Bool)
    (hhalt : (rrun P oracle (Cfg.init l₀ x) N).state = none)
    (hout : (rrun P oracle (Cfg.init l₀ x) N).output = w)
    (hbox : ∀ t ≤ N, ∀ r, lo r ≤ (rrun P oracle (Cfg.init l₀ x) t).workTapePos r ∧
      (rrun P oracle (Cfg.init l₀ x) t).workTapePos r ≤ hi r)
    (hcalls : ∀ t < N, CallOK P D q0 oracle lo hi B (rrun P oracle (Cfg.init l₀ x) t)) :
    ∃ T, (compileFinTM P l₀ D q0).ComputesInTime x w T ∧
      (compileFinTM P l₀ D q0).tm.spaceUsed ((compileFinTM P l₀ D q0).tm.initCfg x) T ≤
        ∑ r, (hi r - lo r + 1).toNat + kD * (2 * B + 1) := by
  obtain ⟨T, hT, hTb⟩ := compile_correct P l₀ D q0 oracle lo hi B N hbox hcalls
  refine ⟨T, ?_, ?_⟩
  · rw [FinTM.computesInTime_iff]
    change ((compileTM P l₀ D q0).runFrom ((compileTM P l₀ D q0).initCfg x) T).state = none ∧
      ((compileTM P l₀ D q0).runFrom ((compileTM P l₀ D q0).initCfg x) T).output = w
    rw [hT]
    exact ⟨by show Option.map _ _ = none; rw [hhalt]; rfl, by show _ = w; exact hout⟩
  · change (compileTM P l₀ D q0).spaceUsed ((compileTM P l₀ D q0).initCfg x) T ≤ _
    have := spaceUsed_le_of_ranges (compileTM P l₀ D q0) ((compileTM P l₀ D q0).initCfg x) T
      (Fin.append lo (fun _ => -(B : ℤ))) (Fin.append hi (fun _ => (B : ℤ))) (by
        intro t ht i
        refine Fin.addCases (fun r => ?_) (fun j => ?_) i
        · simpa using (hTb t ht).1 r
        · have := (hTb t ht).2 j
          simp only [Fin.append_right]
          rw [abs_le] at this
          exact this)
    refine this.trans (le_of_eq ?_)
    rw [Fin.sum_univ_add]
    simp only [Fin.append_left, Fin.append_right, Finset.sum_const, Finset.card_univ,
      Fintype.card_fin, smul_eq_mul]
    congr 1
    congr 1
    omega

end Complexity.LogProg
```

```
/-
Copyright (c) 2026 Seyoon Ragavan. All rights reserved.
Released under Apache 2.0 license as described in the file LICENSE.
Authors: Seyoon Ragavan
-/
import TCSlib.Complexity.SpaceComplexity.ConfigGraph
import TCSlib.Complexity.SpaceComplexity.Constructible
import TCSlib.Complexity.SpaceComplexity.SavitchARM.Correct

set_option maxHeartbeats 0
set_option relaxedAutoImplicit false
set_option autoImplicit false

/-!
# Savitch's theorem

[AB09, Theorem 4.14] ([Sav70]): for space-constructible `S`,
`NSPACE(S(n)) ⊆ SPACE(S(n)²)` — nondeterministic space costs only a quadratic
deterministic overhead, via the midpoint recursion `reach?(u, v, i)` over the
configuration graph of `TCSlib.Complexity.SpaceComplexity.ConfigGraph`. The
corollary `PSPACE = NPSPACE` ([AB09, §4.2.1]) closes the polynomial level.
Phase P4.2 of `AroraBarakChapters3-4Plan.md`.

**Status: partly filled (phase P4.2).** `Complexity.PSPACE_eq_NPSPACE` is
proved, directly at the polynomial level, by the Savitch register machine of
`TCSlib.Complexity.SpaceComplexity.SavitchARM` (`Complexity.NPSPACE_subset_PSPACE`);
`Complexity.savitch` (general space-constructible `S`) and
`Complexity.spaceConstructible_poly` remain sorried with sketches naming their fill
obligations. The `SpaceComplexity.lean` facade has carried this module since the
P4.1 gate closed (root-wired while that gate was live).

## Design

* **The positive-bound convention is respected without side conditions**:
  `Complexity.SpaceConstructible` bundles `logSpace n ≤ S n`, so `S` and
  `S · S` are everywhere positive and the P0-adopted convention
  (`TCSlib.Complexity.SpaceComplexity.ZeroSpace`) imposes no extra hypothesis.
* **The recursion is realized iteratively**: `reach?`'s call stack becomes an
  explicit stack of `O(S)`-bit frames (coded vertices and a midpoint cursor)
  on a dedicated bank, walked by the loop combinator — the §12 layer
  (`Build/Embed.lean`, `Build/Seam.lean`, `Build/Catalog.lean`) is the
  intended engine, with the depth `O(S)` and frame size `O(S)` giving the
  `O(S²)` ledger.

## Main results

* `Complexity.spaceConstructible_poly` — the polynomial bounds of the
  campaign's normal form are space-constructible (degree at least one). (Sorried.)
* `Complexity.savitch` — [AB09, Theorem 4.14]. (Sorried.)
* `Complexity.PSPACE_eq_NPSPACE` — [AB09, §4.2.1]. (Proved.)

## References

* [AB09] S. Arora, B. Barak, *Computational Complexity: A Modern Approach*,
  Cambridge University Press, 2009. (§4.2.1, Theorem 4.14; §4.1.2.)
* [Sav70] W. J. Savitch, *Relationships between nondeterministic and
  deterministic tape complexities*, JCSS 4(2), 1970. (Cited through [AB09];
  no external text is required for this audit.)
-/

namespace Complexity

open Turing

/-- **The campaign's polynomial bounds are space-constructible** (spec, fill
pending — phase P4.2): for `1 ≤ c`, the normal-form bound `n ^ c + 1` is
`Complexity.SpaceConstructible`. (Degree zero is excluded: `n ^ 0 + 1 = 2`
fails the bundled `logSpace n ≤ S n` at large `n`; consumers route degree
zero through monotonicity into degree one.)

**Proof sketch.** Dominance: `logSpace n ≤ n + 1 ≤ n ^ c + 1` for `1 ≤ c`
(`logSpace n ≤ n + 1` by induction on the binary length; `n ≤ n ^ c` for
`n ≥ 1`, and the `n = 0` case is `1 ≤ 1`). The witness machine computes
`(n ^ c + 1).bits` within `O(n ^ c)` visited cells: a unary power bank built
by `c` nested input scans (the `polyUnary` catalog row with its space clause,
`Turing.FinTM.computesFunInTime_polyUnary_spaceUsed`,
`Build/Catalog.lean`), then a unary-to-binary count-down into a binary counter
(`incrementTM`'s discipline; the `polyBits` row's space clause gives the
assembled bound). Named fill obligations: the two catalog instantiations and
the `ComputesInSpace` repackaging of their joint time/space contracts. -/
theorem spaceConstructible_poly (c : ℕ) (hc : 1 ≤ c) :
    SpaceConstructible fun n => n ^ c + 1 := by
  sorry

/-- **Savitch's theorem** ([AB09, Theorem 4.14]; [Sav70]): for
space-constructible `S`, nondeterministic space `S` sits inside deterministic
space `S²`.

**Proof sketch.** Let `N` decide `L` in space `c₀ · S`. Membership is
acceptance within the vertex count
(`Turing.FinNDTM.DecidesInSpace.mem_iff_acceptsWithin_configBound`), i.e.
reachability, in the configuration graph restricted to the window
`[-c₀·S n, c₀·S n]`, from the initial vertex to an accepting one
(`Turing.NDTM.reflTransGen_cfgStep_iff` for the dictionary) within
`V := N.configBound n (c₀·S n)` steps, where `log₂ V = O(S n)` (the
`configBound` exponent arithmetic). The deterministic decider evaluates
`reach?(u, v, i)` — is there a path of length at most `2^i` — by the midpoint
recursion: enumerate midpoints `m` over the coded vertices and recurse on
`(u, m, i - 1)` and `(m, v, i - 1)`, **reusing the space** of the first
recursive call for the second ([AB09]'s crucial point). Realized iteratively:
an explicit stack of at most `log₂ V + 1 = O(S n)` frames, each one coded
vertex pair plus a midpoint cursor of `O(S n)` bits, held on a dedicated bank
and walked with the catalog copy/compare/increment routines under the loop
combinator; one extra bank runs the vertex-adjacency test (one
transition-table application on decoded cores) and the base case. Space:
frames × frame size `= O((S n)²)`, plus `O(S n)` administration — inside
`SPACE (S·S)`'s constant absorption. The initial radius computation is the
constructibility witness, whose own space is `O(S n)`. Named fill
obligations: the frame-stack discipline (a §12 R1/R2 consumer — bank
embedding for the stack bank, seam composition per frame transition), the
midpoint enumerator, the adjacency tester, and the arithmetic packaging
`O(S²) ≤ c' · (S n · S n)`. Positivity of the target bound is automatic
(`S ≥ logSpace ≥ 1`). -/
theorem savitch (S : ℕ → ℕ) (hS : SpaceConstructible S) :
    NSPACE S ⊆ SPACE fun n => S n * S n := by
  sorry

/-- **`PSPACE = NPSPACE`** ([AB09, §4.2.1]; [AB09, Theorem 4.14] at polynomial
space bounds): at the polynomial level, Savitch's quadratic overhead is absorbed.

**Proof sketch.** `⊆` is `Complexity.PSPACE_subset_NPSPACE` (phase P4.1). `⊇` is
`Complexity.NPSPACE_subset_PSPACE`, proved directly rather than through
`Complexity.savitch`: for `N` deciding `L` in space `c (n ^ k + 1)`, take the radius
`s = (n + 2) ^ E` and the code width `w = (n + 2) ^ (2E)` (`E` a constant of `N`, `k`, `c`),
so that the configuration codes of `TCSlib.Complexity.SpaceComplexity.Codec` lie below
`2 ^ w` and the configuration count is at most `2 ^ w`; then `x ∈ L` iff some initial code
reaches some accepting code by the midpoint predicate `REACH(u, v, w)` (paths of length at
most `2 ^ w`, every midpoint a code below `2 ^ w`). The Savitch register machine
(`Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.A`) computes `s`, `w`, `2 ^ w` by counting loops and
evaluates `REACH` by the midpoint recursion, **reusing the space** of the first recursive
call for the second ([AB09]'s crucial point) through an explicit stack: saved endpoints as
`w`-bit digits of one register, phase bits as binary digits of another, so every register
holds at most `w · w` bits. Its deciders (input length and the initial, accepting and step
code languages) are logspace, and `Complexity.LogProg.arm_decides_pspace_val` turns the
machine into a polynomial-space decider. -/
theorem PSPACE_eq_NPSPACE : PSPACE = NPSPACE :=
  Set.Subset.antisymm PSPACE_subset_NPSPACE NPSPACE_subset_PSPACE

end Complexity
```

[AB09, §4.2]: `PSPACE`-hardness and -completeness, the `TQBF` language and
the Stockmeyer-Meyer theorem, and the game-playing face of the class. The
headline statements (phase P4.3 of `AroraBarakChapters3-4Plan.md`) are
`Complexity.TQBF_PSPACEComplete` ([AB09, Theorem 4.13]) with its two halves,
the closed-form configuration codec of Claim 4.4(2) (`Complexity.ConfigCodec`,
restated by RD-2), and Zermelo determinacy for finite perfect-information games
([AB09, Exercise 4.10]).

## Contents

- `ClassPSPACE.TQBF`: Definition 4.9, the collapse corollary, Claim 4.4(2)
  as the closed-form codec `Complexity.ConfigCodec` and its uniform emitters,
  `TQBF`, and Theorem 4.13
- `ClassPSPACE.Games`: finite two-person perfect-information games and
  Zermelo determinacy

import TCSlib.Complexity.Formulas.QBFEncoding
import TCSlib.Complexity.SpaceComplexity.ConfigGraph
import TCSlib.Complexity.SpaceComplexity.Constructible
import TCSlib.Complexity.SpaceComplexity.Inclusions
import TCSlib.Complexity.TuringMachine.Build.CfgRecord
import TCSlib.Complexity.FormulaKit.Gate
import TCSlib.Complexity.FormulaKit.Emit

set_option maxHeartbeats 0
set_option relaxedAutoImplicit false
set_option autoImplicit false

/-!
# `PSPACE`-completeness and `TQBF`

[AB09, §4.2]: `PSPACE`-hardness and -completeness (Definition 4.9), the
adjacency-formula half of Claim 4.4(2), and the Stockmeyer-Meyer theorem that
`TQBF` is `PSPACE`-complete (Theorem 4.13). Phase P4.3 of
`AroraBarakChapters3-4Plan.md`.

## Design

* **Def 4.9 verbatim over the campaign's `≤ₚ`** (`Complexity.PolyTimeReducible`,
  chapter 2); the logspace-reduction variant ([AB09, Exercise 4.9]) waits for
  phase P4.4's `≤ₗ`.
* **Claim 4.4(2) at polynomial size, over the closed-form codec `Complexity.ConfigCodec`**
  (restated by RD-2, user decision of 2026-10-12, `machine-library-design.md` §16b item 2;
  the packaged existential `Complexity.exists_adjacency_codec_cnf` is retired at the RD-2a
  re-fill). For each machine and each `(n, s)`: a configuration bit-codec
  `ConfigCodec.code` of width `ConfigCodec.width M n s = 2n + 4 + Q + 3k(2s + 1)`, linear
  in `s + n`, every field at a closed-form index, **factoring through the input
  and the P4.2 vertex quotient** `Turing.NDTM.coreSum` — full configurations
  are *not* injectively codable at fixed length, the output tape being
  unbounded (round-1 blocker, finding 1) — together with **three** CNFs over
  the code bits, each an explicit clause list ordered by `List.range` and built from the
  truth-table gates of `Complexity.FormulaKit` (design §14 row H6): a validity predicate
  characterizing exactly the codec image (unguarded midpoint quantification admits paths
  through junk codes — round-1 finding 3), the adjacency test (true on same-input windowed
  pairs iff the step descends to the vertex quotient; false across distinct
  inputs), and the acceptance test (halted state with `accept` summary).
